nl:
The system has three kinds of participants: the **Scheduler**, which receives surgery‑booking requests; the **OR‑Manager**, which owns the coarse lock for an entire operating‑room block (e.g., “OR‑1‑Morning”); and the **Equipment‑Agent**, which holds fine‑grained locks for individual pieces of equipment such as a surgical robot or a C‑arm. The Scheduler maintains a variable indicating the current **requested surgery** (including its required equipment list) and a flag showing whether the **room capacity** (number of concurrent cases allowed) has been increased or decreased by the hospital admin. When a new request arrives, the Scheduler first acquires the OR‑Manager’s coarse lock for the target block; once granted it asks each relevant Equipment‑Agent to acquire its fine lock. If any fine lock is denied because the equipment is already in use, the Scheduler releases all previously taken locks, waits for a short back‑off, and retries. When the admin changes the room capacity at runtime, the OR‑Manager updates its capacity flag, and any Scheduler that is waiting at the coarse‑lock stage re‑evaluates whether the block can still admit the new surgery before proceeding. All participants release their locks immediately after the surgery start time is recorded, allowing the next request to use the room and equipment. 

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment, no two surgeries can hold the fine‑grained lock for the same piece of equipment in the same operating‑room block.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C0x8x0x4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Rooms, Equipments

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Types and constants                                                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

NullRoom == "None"               \* a value not belonging to Rooms

Request == [room : Rooms, eqSet : SUBSET Equipments]

NoReq == [room |-> NullRoom, eqSet |-> {}]   \* special value meaning “no pending request”

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Variables                                                          *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

VARIABLES curReq, coarseLock, ActiveSurgeries, capacity

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Initial state                                                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

Init ==
    /\ curReq = NoReq
    /\ coarseLock = [r \in Rooms |-> FALSE]
    /\ ActiveSurgeries = {}
    /\ capacity = 1                \* initial room‑capacity flag (value not used for safety)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Actions                                                            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* A new surgery‑booking request arrives *)
NewRequest ==
    /\ curReq = NoReq
    /\ \E r \in Request :
          /\ curReq' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, ActiveSurgeries, capacity>>

(* Scheduler acquires the coarse lock of the target OR block *)
AcquireCoarse ==
    /\ curReq # NoReq
    /\ coarseLock[curReq.room] = FALSE
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![curReq.room] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curReq, ActiveSurgeries, capacity>>

(* Scheduler successfully acquires all fine‑grained equipment locks *)
AcquireFine ==
    /\ curReq # NoReq
    /\ coarseLock[curReq.room] = TRUE
    /\ \A e \in curReq.eqSet :
          ~(\E s \in ActiveSurgeries :
                s.room = curReq.room /\ e \in s.eqSet)   \* equipment is free in this block
    /\ ActiveSurgeries' = ActiveSurgeries \cup {curReq}
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![curReq.room] = FALSE]
    /\ curReq' = NoReq
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

(* Scheduler fails to acquire at least one fine lock, releases coarse lock *)
FailAcquireFine ==
    /\ curReq # NoReq
    /\ coarseLock[curReq.room] = TRUE
    /\ \E e \in curReq.eqSet :
          (\E s \in ActiveSurgeries :
                s.room = curReq.room /\ e \in s.eqSet)   \* some equipment already held
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![curReq.room] = FALSE]
    /\ curReq' = NoReq
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ActiveSurgeries, capacity>>

(* A surgery starts; all locks for that surgery are released *)
SurgeryStart ==
    /\ \E s \in ActiveSurgeries :
          /\ ActiveSurgeries' = ActiveSurgeries \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, curReq, capacity>>

(* Admin changes the room‑capacity flag (does not affect safety) *)
AdminChangeCapacity ==
    /\ capacity' = IF capacity = 1 THEN 2 ELSE 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<curReq, coarseLock, ActiveSurgeries>>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Next-state relation                                                *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

Next ==
    \/ NewRequest
    \/ AcquireCoarse
    \/ AcquireFine
    \/ FailAcquireFine
    \/ SurgeryStart
    \/ AdminChangeCapacity

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Specification                                                      *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<curReq, coarseLock, ActiveSurgeries, capacity>>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Safety invariant: no two surgeries hold the same equipment lock  *)
(*  in the same operating‑room block.                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

SafetyInvariant ==
    \A s1 \in ActiveSurgeries :
        \A s2 \in ActiveSurgeries :
            (s1 /= s2) => (s1.room /= s2.room) \/ (s1.eqSet \cap s2.eqSet = {})

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(*  Theorem (for TLC)                                                  *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

THEOREM Spec => []SafetyInvariant

====

The system involves three roles: a Patron who submits reservation requests, a ReservationManager that queues and schedules those requests, and a NotificationWorker that finalizes reservations and sends confirmation emails. The ReservationManager keeps a bounded work queue whose size is limited to a fixed capacity. When a Patron adds a request, the manager tries to place it in the queue; if the queue is already full, the manager returns a back‑pressure signal and asks the patron to retry later. The NotificationWorker repeatedly removes the oldest request from the queue, marks the requested book as reserved, and dispatches a confirmation; after each successful step it deletes the request from the queue. Because the worker may be slow but never fails, the queue can temporarily fill, causing back‑pressure to flow back to patrons, but no request is ever lost. The manager never drops a request; it simply retains it in the queue until the worker has processed it. The whole system’s state can be represented with two variables: the current number of items in the queue and the reservation status of each book.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of reservation requests stored in the queue never exceeds its configured maximum capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4C19x4x4x3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS  Books, MaxCap

VARIABLES queue, reserved

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Helper definitions *)
QueueLen == Len(queue)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ queue   = << >>
    /\ reserved = {}

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Actions *)

(* A patron adds a reservation request for book b.
   The manager accepts it only if there is spare capacity. *)
AddRequest(b) ==
    /\ b \in Books
    /\ QueueLen < MaxCap
    /\ queue'   = Append(queue, b)
    /\ UNCHANGED reserved

(* The notification worker processes the oldest request.
   It removes the head of the queue and marks the corresponding book reserved. *)
Process ==
    /\ QueueLen > 0
    /\ LET b == Head(queue) IN
          /\ queue'    = Tail(queue)
          /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {b}

(* The overall next-state relation *)
Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Books : AddRequest(b)
    \/ Process

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Safety invariant: the queue never exceeds its configured capacity *)
QueueCapInv == QueueLen <= MaxCap

(* (Optional) type-correctness invariant – not used for the required safety check *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Books)
    /\ reserved \subseteq Books
    /\ QueueLen <= MaxCap

=============================================================================

The system consists of three agents: a RunwayController that manages the whole runway, several TaxiControllers that manage individual landing‑or‑take‑off slots, and a privileged Admin that can intervene at any time. The RunwayController holds a coarse lock called runwayLock which, when held, guarantees exclusive access to the runway’s overall capacity. A TaxiController must first acquire runwayLock, then a fine‑grained lock called slotLock that corresponds to a specific time slot before it can assign an aircraft to that slot. After the aircraft has landed or taken off, the TaxiController releases its slotLock while keeping runwayLock until all of its pending updates are finished, then it releases runwayLock. The Admin can pre‑empt any holder of runwayLock or slotLock by issuing an override command; when this occurs the locks are instantly transferred to the Admin, who may reset the allocation or clear a slot. All agents periodically read the shared state variable currentAllocation, which records the number of occupied slots, to decide whether a new request can be accepted. If an override is in effect, normal agents must wait until the Admin clears the override before attempting to reacquire any lock.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time will the number of aircraft assigned to runway slots exceed the runway’s maximum capacity.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C1x8x4x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Constants
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
CONSTANTS TaxiIds, Slots, Capacity

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Simple identifiers for special owners
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
None  == "None"
Admin == "Admin"

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Variables
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
VARIABLES runwayLock, slotLocks, currentAllocation, override

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  State predicates
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
Init ==
    /\ runwayLock = None
    /\ slotLocks = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ currentAllocation = 0
    /\ override = FALSE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  TaxiController actions
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
AcquireRunway(t) ==
    /\ t \in TaxiIds
    /\ runwayLock = None
    /\ ~override
    /\ runwayLock' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLocks, currentAllocation, override>>

AcquireSlot(t, s) ==
    /\ t \in TaxiIds
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ runwayLock = t
    /\ slotLocks[s] = None
    /\ ~override
    /\ slotLocks' = [slotLocks EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayLock, currentAllocation, override>>

AssignAircraft(t, s) ==
    /\ t \in TaxiIds
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ slotLocks[s] = t
    /\ currentAllocation < Capacity
    /\ currentAllocation' = currentAllocation + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayLock, slotLocks, override>>

ReleaseSlot(t, s) ==
    /\ t \in TaxiIds
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ slotLocks[s] = t
    /\ currentAllocation > 0
    /\ slotLocks' = [slotLocks EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ currentAllocation' = currentAllocation - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayLock, override>>

ReleaseRunway(t) ==
    /\ t \in TaxiIds
    /\ runwayLock = t
    /\ \A s \in Slots: slotLocks[s] = None
    /\ runwayLock' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLocks, currentAllocation, override>>

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Admin actions
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
AdminOverride ==
    /\ ~override
    /\ override' = TRUE
    /\ runwayLock' = Admin
    /\ slotLocks' = [s \in Slots |-> IF slotLocks[s] # None THEN Admin ELSE None]
    /\ UNCHANGED currentAllocation

AdminClearOverride ==
    /\ override
    /\ override' = FALSE
    /\ runwayLock' = None
    /\ slotLocks' = [s \in Slots |-> None]
    /\ UNCHANGED currentAllocation

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Next-state relation
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
Next ==
    \/ \E t \in TaxiIds: AcquireRunway(t)
    \/ \E t \in TaxiIds, s \in Slots: AcquireSlot(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in TaxiIds, s \in Slots: AssignAircraft(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in TaxiIds, s \in Slots: ReleaseSlot(t, s)
    \/ \E t \in TaxiIds: ReleaseRunway(t)
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ AdminClearOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<runwayLock, slotLocks, currentAllocation, override>>

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Safety invariant
  --------------------------------------------------------------------*)
CapacityInvariant == currentAllocation <= Capacity

=============================================================================

The system consists of a Train Controller that requests a block, a Signal Block that records whether it is free, occupied or pending, and a small quorum of three Quorum Agents that exchange votes. Each participant stores a single variable: the Block’s status (free/occupied/pending) and a vote flag (yes/no) that the agents use when a request arrives. When a controller wants to enter a block, it broadcasts a *request* message to all quorum agents and sets the block’s status to pending. Each quorum agent, upon receiving the request, replies with a yes vote after confirming that the block’s status is still free; a slow agent may delay its reply but never crashes. When the controller collects a majority of yes votes, it sends a *commit* message, all agents update their vote flag to committed and the block’s status changes irrevocably to occupied. If the controller does not achieve a majority within a timeout, it aborts the request, resets the block’s status to free, and the quorum agents discard any pending votes. Once a block is marked occupied, no subsequent request can transition it to occupied again until a separate *release* action clears it back to free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A block can be set to occupied at most once before it is cleared.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C10x5x5x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Agents

VARIABLES status, vote, occCount

(* The possible values for the block status *)
StatusVals == {"free", "pending", "occupied"}

(* The possible values for a quorum agent's vote flag *)
VoteVals == {"none", "yes", "committed"}

(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ status = "free"
    /\ vote = [a \in Agents |-> "none"]
    /\ occCount = 0

(* Controller issues a request: block becomes pending, votes cleared *)
Request ==
    /\ status = "free"
    /\ status' = "pending"
    /\ vote' = [a \in Agents |-> "none"]
    /\ occCount' = occCount

(* A single quorum agent a votes "yes" while the request is pending *)
AgentVote(a) ==
    /\ a \in Agents
    /\ status = "pending"
    /\ vote[a] = "none"
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![a] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << status, occCount >>

(* The set of agents that have voted yes *)
YesVotes == {a \in Agents : vote[a] = "yes"}

(* Controller commits when it has a majority of yes votes and no prior occupancy *)
Commit ==
    /\ status = "pending"
    /\ Cardinality(YesVotes) >= 2
    /\ occCount = 0
    /\ status' = "occupied"
    /\ occCount' = occCount + 1
    /\ vote' = [a \in Agents |-> "committed"]

(* Controller aborts if it cannot obtain a majority *)
Abort ==
    /\ status = "pending"
    /\ Cardinality(YesVotes) < 2
    /\ status' = "free"
    /\ vote' = [a \in Agents |-> "none"]
    /\ occCount' = occCount

(* Release clears the occupied block *)
Release ==
    /\ status = "occupied"
    /\ status' = "free"
    /\ vote' = [a \in Agents |-> "none"]
    /\ occCount' = 0

(* The overall step relation *)
Next ==
    \/ Request
    \/ \E a \in Agents: AgentVote(a)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Release

(* Safety invariant: at most one occupancy before a release *)
OccCountBound == occCount <= 1

====

The system has two settlement processors, Processor A and Processor B, each responsible for collecting a batch of inter‑bank transfers before committing them to the shared clearing pool. Both processors keep a local counter of how many transfers they have already placed in the pool, and they also read a single global compare‑and‑swap register that stores the current total number of entries in the pool. When a processor is ready to add a new transfer, it first reads the register; if the read value plus the local counter would stay below the pool’s maximum capacity, it attempts a compare‑and‑swap that atomically updates the register from the old total to the new total. If the compare‑and‑swap succeeds, the processor records the transfer locally and increments its counter; if it fails, the processor re‑reads the register and retries the check. Because the two processors share the same register, only one of them can succeed in updating the total for any given transfer, preventing over‑commit. The protocol repeats until each processor’s batch is either fully committed or rejected when the pool is full. 

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of transfers recorded in the shared clearing pool never exceeds its configured capacity.

---- MODULE W4C3x7x4x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANT Capacity

VARIABLES reg, localA, localB

(* ---- Initialization ---- *)
Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ localA = 0
    /\ localB = 0

(* ---- Processor A tries to commit one transfer ---- *)
AAdd ==
    /\ reg < Capacity               \* there is room in the pool
    /\ reg' = reg + 1               \* successful CAS updates the total
    /\ localA' = localA + 1         \* record the transfer locally
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localB>>

(* ---- Processor B tries to commit one transfer ---- *)
BAdd ==
    /\ reg < Capacity
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ localB' = localB + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localA>>

(* ---- Stuttering step – no processor makes progress ---- *)
Stutter ==
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, localA, localB>>

Next ==
    AAdd \/ BAdd \/ Stutter

Spec ==
    Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, localA, localB>>

(* ---- Safety invariant: the pool never exceeds its capacity ---- *)
Safe ==
    reg <= Capacity

=============================================================================

INVARIANT Safe

nl:
The swarm consists of a set of autonomous fire‑monitoring drones (called **Nodes**) and a ground control station that hosts the **Epoch Manager**. Each Node stores two pieces of state: the current **epoch number** and the identifier of the **active flight plan** assigned for that epoch. When the Epoch Manager decides to reconfigure the swarm—e.g., to add a new sensor payload or to redirect coverage—it increments the epoch number, publishes a signed **epoch update** containing the new flight plan, and broadcasts it to all Nodes. Upon receiving a signed update, a Node validates the signature, discards any older epoch, installs the new flight plan, and acknowledges the change back to the Epoch Manager. A privileged **Admin Console** can issue an **override command** that carries a higher‑level signature; this command replaces the pending epoch update and forces all Nodes to adopt the override flight plan immediately, regardless of their current epoch. Nodes only act on a flight plan after they have stored the matching epoch number or an admin override that they have verified. The epoch‑numbered reconfiguration thus provides a simple, monotonic coordination mechanism while still allowing the admin to pre‑empt it in emergencies.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No drone may execute a surveillance maneuver or accept a reconfiguration unless it holds the most recent epoch number or a valid admin‑override signature, preventing actions by unauthorized or stale participants.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4C14x9x6x5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* CONSTANTS *)
CONSTANTS
    Nodes,      \* Finite set of drone identifiers
    Plans,      \* Finite set of possible flight‑plan identifiers
    MaxEpoch    \* Upper bound on epoch numbers (inclusive)

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* VARIABLES *)
VARIABLES
    epoch,          \* current epoch number (0 .. MaxEpoch)
    globalPlan,    \* flight plan associated with the current epoch
    nodeEpoch,     \* [n \in Nodes |-> epoch stored at node n]
    nodePlan,      \* [n \in Nodes |-> flight plan stored at node n]
    overrideActive,\* TRUE iff an admin‑override is in effect
    overridePlan,  \* flight plan supplied by the admin‑override
    nodeOverride,  \* [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE iff node n follows admin‑override]
    exec           \* [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE iff node n is executing a maneuver]

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Helper definitions *)
IsLatestEpoch(n) == nodeEpoch[n] = epoch
IsOverridden(n)   == nodeOverride[n]

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ globalPlan \in Plans
    /\ nodeEpoch = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ nodePlan = [n \in Nodes |-> globalPlan]
    /\ overrideActive = FALSE
    /\ overridePlan \in Plans
    /\ nodeOverride = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
    /\ exec = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Epoch manager issues a new epoch‑numbered reconfiguration *)
EpochTick ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ LET newEpoch == epoch + 1
           newPlan  == CHOOSE p \in Plans : TRUE
       IN
          /\ epoch' = newEpoch
          /\ globalPlan' = newPlan
          /\ overrideActive' = FALSE
          /\ overridePlan' = CHOOSE p \in Plans : TRUE
          /\ nodeEpoch' = [n \in Nodes |-> newEpoch]
          /\ nodePlan' = [n \in Nodes |-> newPlan]
          /\ nodeOverride' = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
          /\ exec' = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Admin console issues an override that pre‑empts the pending epoch *)
AdminOverride ==
    /\ LET newPlan == CHOOSE p \in Plans : TRUE
       IN
          /\ overrideActive' = TRUE
          /\ overridePlan' = newPlan
          /\ nodeOverride' = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
          /\ nodePlan' = [n \in Nodes |-> newPlan]
          /\ exec' = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
          /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, globalPlan, nodeEpoch>>

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* A node starts executing a surveillance maneuver *)
Execute(n) ==
    /\ n \in Nodes
    /\ exec[n] = FALSE
    /\ (IsOverridden(n) \/ IsLatestEpoch(n))    \* safety pre‑condition
    /\ exec' = [m \in Nodes |-> IF m = n THEN TRUE ELSE exec[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, globalPlan, nodeEpoch, nodePlan,
                   overrideActive, overridePlan, nodeOverride>>

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* The system's possible next steps *)
Next ==
    \/ EpochTick
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Execute(n)

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Specification *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, globalPlan, nodeEpoch, nodePlan,
                               overrideActive, overridePlan,
                               nodeOverride, exec>>

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Safety invariant: a node may execute only if it holds the latest
   epoch number or a valid admin‑override *)
SafetyInvariant ==
    \A n \in Nodes :
        exec[n] => (IsOverridden(n) \/ IsLatestEpoch(n))

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
THEOREM Spec => []SafetyInvariant
=====================================================================

nl:
The system consists of a set of regional Load Controllers (LCs) that each manage a cluster of substations, and a single Vote Pool that holds a fixed number of voting tokens. Each LC keeps two pieces of state: a flag indicating whether it is currently participating in a load‑shed proposal, and a boolean that records whether it has a token borrowed from the Vote Pool. When a LC detects an overload it starts a shed proposal, requests one token from the pool, and broadcasts the desired reduction amount to the other LCs. The other LCs, upon receiving the proposal, may cast a “yes” vote by attaching their own token; a proposal is executed once a quorum (more than half of the tokens in the pool) have voted “yes”. After the load is actually shed, every participating LC returns its token to the Vote Pool and clears its participation flag. Because two independent shedding instances share the same pool, a token that is still held for one instance cannot be borrowed by the other, preventing more than one quorum from forming simultaneously. The protocol repeats for subsequent overload events, always respecting the token bookkeeping rules.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of voting tokens in the shared pool plus the tokens currently held by all Load Controllers is invariant and never changes.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C9x5x2x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS LCs, TokenCount

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Variables
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
VARIABLES pool, participating, heldTokens

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Definitions
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Tokens currently free in the vote pool *)
Pool == pool

(* Set of load controllers that are currently participating in a proposal *)
Participating == participating

(* Set of load controllers that currently hold a token from the pool *)
HeldTokens == heldTokens

(* Quorum is more than half of the total tokens *)
Quorum == TokenCount \div 2 + 1

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Initial state
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
Init ==
    /\ pool = TokenCount
    /\ participating = {}
    /\ heldTokens = {}

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Actions
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* A load controller detects overload and starts a new proposal,
   borrowing a token from the pool. *)
Start(lc) ==
    /\ lc \in LCs
    /\ lc \notin participating
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ participating' = participating \cup {lc}
    /\ heldTokens' = heldTokens \cup {lc}
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>   \* no other variables

(* Another load controller votes “yes” on an already‑started proposal,
   also borrowing a token. *)
Vote(lc) ==
    /\ lc \in LCs
    /\ lc \notin participating
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ participating' = participating \cup {lc}
    /\ heldTokens' = heldTokens \cup {lc}
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>   \* no other variables

(* When a quorum of tokens has been gathered, the proposal is executed.
   All participating controllers return their tokens and clear their flags. *)
Execute ==
    /\ Cardinality(heldTokens) >= Quorum
    /\ pool' = pool + Cardinality(heldTokens)
    /\ participating' = {}
    /\ heldTokens' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>   \* no other variables

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Next-state relation
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
Next ==
    \/ \E lc \in LCs : Start(lc)
    \/ \E lc \in LCs : Vote(lc)
    \/ Execute

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Specification
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
Spec ==
    Init /\ [][Next]_<<pool, participating, heldTokens>>

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------
  Safety invariant: total number of tokens is constant
--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
TokenInvariant ==
    pool + Cardinality(heldTokens) = TokenCount

=============================================================================

nl:
The scheduler runs on a set of nodes that each represent a participant: a surgeon, an anesthesiologist, a nursing coordinator, and a central OR manager. Each participant keeps a tiny local record of two flags – whether it currently holds the coarse lock for an operating‑room block (e.g., “OR‑A‑Block”) and whether it holds the fine lock for a specific resource such as the laparoscopic tower. To start a surgery the surgeon first requests the coarse lock for the chosen block; once granted the central manager records the block as “reserved”. After the coarse lock is obtained, the nurse requests the fine lock for the needed equipment; the manager only grants it while the block lock is still held, preventing two surgeries from sharing the same equipment. If any participant takes longer than expected (for example, the anesthesiologist is delayed), it simply holds its locks longer; the protocol does not abort the whole operation but allows other participants to continue once they have released their own locks. When the procedure finishes, each participant releases its fine lock, then the surgeon releases the coarse block lock, and the manager clears the reservation. The hierarchical lock ordering guarantees that a slow participant cannot cause a dead‑end where a later surgery proceeds with resources that have not been safely reserved. 

SAFETY PROPERTY: No surgery can start using an operating‑room or equipment unless the participant that holds the coarse block lock has also granted the fine lock, preventing any unauthorized or stale access.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C0x8x6x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

CONSTANTS Participants

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, reserved

(* type constraints *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ coarseLock \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ fineLock   \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reserved   \in BOOLEAN

(* initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
    /\ fineLock   = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
    /\ reserved   = FALSE

(* actions *)

SurgeonRequestsCoarse ==
    /\ ~coarseLock["Surgeon"]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT !["Surgeon"] = TRUE]
    /\ reserved'   = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED fineLock

NurseRequestsFine ==
    /\ coarseLock["Surgeon"]
    /\ ~fineLock["Nurse"]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT !["Nurse"] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, reserved>>

AnesthesiologistRequestsFine ==
    /\ coarseLock["Surgeon"]
    /\ ~fineLock["Anesthesiologist"]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT !["Anesthesiologist"] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, reserved>>

ReleaseFine(p) ==
    /\ p \in Participants
    /\ fineLock[p]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, reserved>>

SurgeonReleasesCoarse ==
    /\ coarseLock["Surgeon"]
    /\ \A p \in Participants : ~fineLock[p]   \* all fine locks released
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT !["Surgeon"] = FALSE]
    /\ reserved'   = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED fineLock

Next ==
    \/ SurgeonRequestsCoarse
    \/ NurseRequestsFine
    \/ AnesthesiologistRequestsFine
    \/ \E p \in Participants : ReleaseFine(p)
    \/ SurgeonReleasesCoarse

(* safety invariant: a fine lock may be held only while the coarse block lock is held
   and the manager’s reservation is active *)
SafeFineUse ==
    \A p \in Participants :
        fineLock[p] => (coarseLock["Surgeon"] /\ reserved)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, fineLock, reserved>>
====

INIT Init

nl:
The line controller first obtains a coarse lock on the entire conveyor segment that a car is about to enter, preventing any other controller from assigning a new car to that segment. While holding the coarse lock, the controller then requests a fine lock on the specific wash‑bay slot (e.g., “Bay 3”) that it plans to use for the car. Each wash‑bay sensor acknowledges the fine‑lock request and records the car’s identifier, but because messages may be reordered, the controller re‑checks the sensor’s acknowledgment before proceeding to the next step. After both locks are confirmed, the controller sends a “move‑forward” command to the conveyor motor; the motor only acts if it still sees the coarse lock active. Once the car reaches the bay, the bay’s water‑spray module acquires its own internal lock, performs the wash cycle, and then releases the fine lock. Finally, the controller releases the coarse conveyor lock, allowing the next car to be scheduled. All participants periodically broadcast their lock state so that any out‑of‑order messages can be ignored if they refer to a lock that has already been released.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No wash‑bay slot is ever assigned to more than one car at the same time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C4x8x3x1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, TLC

CONSTANTS Cars, Bays, Controllers

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments

(* A distinguished value meaning “no lock / no car”. *)
Null == "null"

(* ---------- Initialization ---------- *)
Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = Null
    /\ fineLock = [b \in Bays |-> Null]
    /\ sensorAck = [b \in Bays |-> Null]
    /\ bayAssignments = {}

(* ---------- Actions ---------- *)

(* A controller grabs the coarse lock for the whole segment. *)
ObtainCoarseLock(c) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ coarseLock = Null
    /\ coarseLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments >>

(* While holding the coarse lock, the controller asks a specific bay for a fine lock.
   The bay’s sensor records the car identifier. *)
RequestFineLock(c, b, car) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Bays
    /\ car \in Cars
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ fineLock[b] = Null
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ sensorAck' = [sensorAck EXCEPT ![b] = car]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseLock, bayAssignments >>

(* The controller re‑checks the sensor acknowledgment (messages may be reordered). *)
SensorAckCheck(c, b, car) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Bays
    /\ car \in Cars
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ fineLock[b] = c
    /\ sensorAck[b] = car
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseLock, fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments >>

(* After both locks are confirmed the controller tells the motor to move the car forward. *)
MoveForward(c, b, car) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Bays
    /\ car \in Cars
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ fineLock[b] = c
    /\ sensorAck[b] = car
    /\ <<b, car>> \notin bayAssignments
    /\ bayAssignments' = bayAssignments \cup {<<b, car>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseLock, fineLock, sensorAck >>

(* The wash‑bay’s water‑spray module performs the wash (abstracted). *)
WashCycle(b, car) ==
    /\ b \in Bays
    /\ car \in Cars
    /\ <<b, car>> \in bayAssignments
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseLock, fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments >>

(* The bay releases its fine lock after the wash is done. *)
ReleaseFineLock(c, b, car) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Bays
    /\ car \in Cars
    /\ fineLock[b] = c
    /\ <<b, car>> \in bayAssignments
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![b] = Null]
    /\ sensorAck' = [sensorAck EXCEPT ![b] = Null]
    /\ bayAssignments' = bayAssignments \ {<<b, car>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

(* Finally the controller releases the coarse lock, allowing the next car to be scheduled. *)
ReleaseCoarseLock(c) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ \A b \in Bays : fineLock[b] = Null
    /\ coarseLock' = Null
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments >>

(* ---------- Next-state relation ---------- *)
Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ObtainCoarseLock(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Bays, car \in Cars : RequestFineLock(c, b, car)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Bays, car \in Cars : SensorAckCheck(c, b, car)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Bays, car \in Cars : MoveForward(c, b, car)
    \/ \E b \in Bays, car \in Cars : WashCycle(b, car)          \* optional, does not change state
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Bays, car \in Cars : ReleaseFineLock(c, b, car)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : ReleaseCoarseLock(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, fineLock, sensorAck, bayAssignments>>

(* ---------- Safety invariant ----------
   No wash‑bay slot is ever assigned to more than one car at the same time. *)
NoDoubleAssign ==
    \A b \in Bays :
        \A c1, c2 \in Cars :
            (<<b, c1>> \in bayAssignments /\ <<b, c2>> \in bayAssignments) => c1 = c2

=============================================================================

nl:
The system consists of three signal controllers – North, Central and South – each responsible for one block of the line, and a central administrative console that can issue an override.  
Each controller keeps a local copy of the block’s “clearance level” (closed, approach, or cleared) and a flag indicating whether it has voted on the most recent requested change.  
When a train approaches a block, the controller that detects the train proposes a new clearance level and broadcasts the proposal to the other two controllers.  
The three controllers then exchange votes; the proposal is committed only when at least two controllers have voted “accept”, at which point each updates its local clearance level to the new value.  
If an admin issues an override through the console, the override carries a special “override” flag; the console’s message is automatically counted as two votes, so a single controller’s dissent is insufficient to block the change.  
When an override is accepted, all controllers replace their clearance level with the admin‑specified value, regardless of their previous votes, and reset their vote flags.  
If the quorum is not reached within a timeout, the proposal is aborted and the controllers retain their previous clearance level.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two controllers ever record different clearance levels for the same block at the same logical time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C10x5x1x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers

VARIABLES clearance, hasProp, propBlock, propLevel, propVotes

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Domain definitions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Levels == {"closed", "approach", "cleared"}

Blocks == Controllers          \* each controller maintains a copy for each block

NoBlock == ""                 \* placeholder used when there is no active proposal

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ clearance = [c \in Controllers |-> [b \in Blocks |-> "closed"]]
    /\ hasProp   = FALSE
    /\ propBlock = NoBlock
    /\ propLevel = NoBlock
    /\ propVotes = {}

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Propose(c, b, l) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Blocks
    /\ l \in Levels
    /\ hasProp = FALSE                     \* no outstanding proposal
    /\ hasProp'   = TRUE
    /\ propBlock' = b
    /\ propLevel' = l
    /\ propVotes' = {c}                    \* proposer implicitly votes accept
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clearance>>

Vote(c) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ hasProp = TRUE
    /\ c \notin propVotes
    /\ hasProp'   = TRUE
    /\ propVotes' = propVotes \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clearance, propBlock, propLevel>>

Commit ==
    /\ hasProp = TRUE
    /\ Cardinality(propVotes) >= 2        \* quorum reached
    /\ hasProp'   = FALSE
    /\ propBlock' = NoBlock
    /\ propLevel' = NoBlock
    /\ propVotes' = {}
    /\ clearance' = [c \in Controllers |-> 
          [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = propBlock THEN propLevel ELSE clearance[c][b]]]

Override(c, b, l) ==
    /\ c \in Controllers
    /\ b \in Blocks
    /\ l \in Levels
    /\ hasProp'   = FALSE                  \* any pending proposal is discarded
    /\ propBlock' = NoBlock
    /\ propLevel' = NoBlock
    /\ propVotes' = {}
    /\ clearance' = [c2 \in Controllers |-> 
          [b2 \in Blocks |-> IF b2 = b THEN l ELSE clearance[c2][b2]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<>>

Abort ==
    /\ hasProp = TRUE
    /\ hasProp'   = FALSE
    /\ propBlock' = NoBlock
    /\ propLevel' = NoBlock
    /\ propVotes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED clearance

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Next-state relation
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks, l \in Levels: Propose(c, b, l)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers: Vote(c)
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks, l \in Levels: Override(c, b, l)
    \/ Abort

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<clearance, hasProp, propBlock, propLevel, propVotes>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety invariant (the property from the natural‑language description)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Consistent ==
    \A b \in Blocks: \A c1, c2 \in Controllers: clearance[c1][b] = clearance[c2][b]

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANT Controllers = {"North", "Central", "South"}

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Consistent

nl:
The system consists of a Grid Operator (the coordinator) and a set of Substation Controllers that each manage a local load‑shedding actuator. Each Substation Controller maintains a binary flag “prepared” that indicates it has verified that its local loads can be shed, and a vote (“ready” or “abort”) it will send back to the Grid Operator. The Grid Operator runs a two‑phase commit: in the first phase it broadcasts a shed request, collects votes, and if all are “ready” it moves to a pre‑commit stage where it atomically reserves the required megawatts from the Shared Load Pool. In the second phase the Grid Operator issues a commit message, the Substation Controllers then execute the actual disconnection of their assigned loads, and finally the reserved megawatts are deducted from the pool. Two independent load‑shed instances (for example “day‑time” and “emergency”) share the same pool, so each instance must first check that the pool has enough free megawatts before entering the pre‑commit stage, preventing double‑reservation across instances. If any controller votes “abort”, the Grid Operator aborts the transaction, releases any provisional reservations, and the pool state is left unchanged. All messages are asynchronous but the two‑phase commit guarantees that either all controllers shed their loads or none do, even when both instances are active concurrently.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A megawatt of load is physically disconnected by a substation at most once for any given load‑shed instance.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C9x2x5x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Substations, Instances, TotalPool

VARIABLES pool, reserved, committed, state, vote, prepared, disconnectCount

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Helper definitions *)

Needed == Cardinality(Substations) \* each substation sheds 1 MW

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Initialization *)

Init ==
    /\ pool = TotalPool
    /\ reserved = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ committed = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ state = [i \in Instances |-> "idle"]
    /\ vote = [i \in Instances |-> [s \in Substations |-> "ready"]]
    /\ prepared = [i \in Instances |-> [s \in Substations |-> FALSE]]
    /\ disconnectCount = [i \in Instances |-> [s \in Substations |-> 0]]

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Actions *)

Request(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "idle"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "collect"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

Prepare(s,i) ==
    /\ s \in Substations /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "collect"
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![i][s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, state, vote, disconnectCount>>

Vote(s,i,v) ==
    /\ s \in Substations /\ i \in Instances /\ v \in {"ready","abort"}
    /\ state[i] = "collect"
    /\ prepared[i][s] = TRUE
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![i][s] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, state, prepared, disconnectCount>>

Collect(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "collect"
    /\ \A s \in Substations: vote[i][s] # "abort"      \* all votes are “ready”
    /\ pool >= Needed                                 \* enough free MW
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "precommit"]
    /\ pool' = pool - Needed
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = Needed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

AbortCollect(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "collect"
    /\ \E s \in Substations: vote[i][s] = "abort"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "precommit"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "commit"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

Disconnect(s,i) ==
    /\ s \in Substations /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "commit"
    /\ disconnectCount[i][s] = 0
    /\ disconnectCount' = [disconnectCount EXCEPT ![i][s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserved, committed, state, vote, prepared>>

Finish(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "commit"
    /\ \A s \in Substations: disconnectCount[i][s] = 1
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![i] = committed[i] + reserved[i]]
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

AbortPre(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ state[i] = "precommit"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ pool' = pool + reserved[i]
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Next-state relation *)

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances: Request(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Substations: Prepare(s,i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Substations, v \in {"ready","abort"}: Vote(s,i,v)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: Collect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: AbortCollect(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: Commit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Substations: Disconnect(s,i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: Finish(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: AbortPre(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<pool, reserved, committed, state, vote, prepared, disconnectCount>>

(* -------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Safety invariant: a megawatt is disconnected at most once per instance *)

NoDoubleDisconnect ==
    \A i \in Instances: \A s \in Substations: disconnectCount[i][s] <= 1

=============================================================================

The system has three participants: aircraft controllers that request runway time, a runway manager that keeps the lock state for each runway, and a privileged admin that can pre‑empt any lock.  
The runway manager maintains a coarse lock indicating whether a runway is globally free or reserved, and a fine lock that records which specific aircraft currently holds the runway.  
When a controller wants to land, it first acquires the coarse lock for the desired runway; if successful it then acquires the fine lock for its own aircraft identifier.  
If the coarse lock is already held, the controller must wait, and it examines the fine lock only after the coarse lock has been obtained, preserving the hierarchical ordering.  
At any moment the admin may issue an override that instantly clears both the coarse and fine locks for a runway, forcing all pending controllers to restart their acquisition sequence.  
After a controller has obtained both locks it signals “runway allocated” and later releases the fine lock when the aircraft vacates, after which the coarse lock is released when no other fine locks remain.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway is assigned to a specific aircraft at most once before that aircraft releases the runway.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C1x8x5x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANTS Runways, Aircraft

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Constants, auxiliary definitions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
NONE == "None" \* special value meaning “no aircraft”

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Variables
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, history

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Type invariant (helps TLC, not the safety property we are checking)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeOK ==
    /\ coarseLock \in [Runways -> {"Free","Reserved"}]
    /\ fineLock   \in [Runways -> Aircraft \cup {NONE}]
    /\ history    \in [Runways -> Aircraft \cup {NONE}]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [r \in Runways |-> "Free"]
    /\ fineLock   = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]
    /\ history    = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Controller actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
AcquireCoarse(a, r) ==
    /\ a \in Aircraft
    /\ r \in Runways
    /\ coarseLock[r] = "Free"
    /\ fineLock[r] = NONE
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = "Reserved"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineLock, history >>

AcquireFine(a, r) ==
    /\ a \in Aircraft
    /\ r \in Runways
    /\ coarseLock[r] = "Reserved"
    /\ fineLock[r] = NONE
    /\ history[r] # a          \* hierarchical ordering – cannot reacquire same aircraft consecutively
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseLock, history >>

ReleaseFine(a, r) ==
    /\ a \in Aircraft
    /\ r \in Runways
    /\ fineLock[r] = a
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ history'  = [history EXCEPT ![r] = a]
    /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

ReleaseCoarse(r) ==
    /\ r \in Runways
    /\ coarseLock[r] = "Reserved"
    /\ fineLock[r] = NONE
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = "Free"]
    /\ history' = [history EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED fineLock

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Admin action
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
AdminOverride(r) ==
    /\ r \in Runways
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![r] = "Free"]
    /\ fineLock'   = [fineLock   EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ history'    = [history    EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Next-state relation
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : AcquireCoarse(a, r)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : AcquireFine(a, r)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft, r \in Runways : ReleaseFine(a, r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways               : ReleaseCoarse(r)
    \/ \E r \in Runways               : AdminOverride(r)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Safety invariant (the property we must check)
\*   “A runway is assigned to a specific aircraft at most once before that
\*    aircraft releases the runway.”
\*   Expressed as: if a runway currently holds a fine lock for aircraft a,
\*   then the most‑recently released aircraft for that runway is different
\*   from a (i.e., a cannot reacquire without a prior release).
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Inv ==
    \A r \in Runways :
        IF fineLock[r] # NONE
        THEN history[r] # fineLock[r]
        ELSE TRUE

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\*   Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, fineLock, history>>

THEOREM Spec => []Inv

====

nl:
The system has three kinds of participants: (1) two independent print‑job submitters, each running in its own instance, (2) a shared pool of printer workers, and (3) a bounded work queue that holds at most N pending jobs.  
Each submitter keeps a local counter of how many of its own jobs are currently in the queue, while the queue maintains a single integer “size” representing the total number of enqueued jobs.  
When a submitter wants to add a new job, it first checks that its local counter is below a per‑client limit and that the queue’s size is less than N; if both checks succeed it increments its counter and the queue size and places the job into the queue.  
If the queue is full, the submitter must wait (backpressure) until a worker removes a job, at which point the queue size is decremented and the worker notifies the originating submitter to decrement its local counter.  
Workers repeatedly dequeue the oldest job, print it, and then signal the submitter that created the job so that the submitter can update its counter.  
Because both submitters share the same queue, the backpressure mechanism guarantees that neither instance can overflow the queue or exceed its own per‑client limit.  
All state updates are atomic: the queue size, the per‑client counters, and the dequeue operation are performed together so that the system never observes an intermediate inconsistent state.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No job is ever printed that was submitted by a client that has not successfully reserved a slot in the shared bounded queue.

nl:
The warehouse runs two identical fleet‑manager instances, each controlling a set of Picker robots that fetch items from shelves and a set of Loader robots that place the items onto delivery pallets. All robots share a single TaskPool that contains a list of pending pick‑tasks, each task entry storing the ID of the robot currently assigned (or “none”) and a version counter. When a robot wants to start a task it reads the task entry and its version, writes its own ID into the entry only if the version it saw is still current, and then increments the version; this is the optimistic‑lock “claim” step. If the write fails because another robot has updated the version in the meantime, the robot discards the stale data and retries the whole claim sequence with the latest version. After a robot successfully claims a task, it proceeds to the execution phase, and once the item is placed on a pallet the robot marks the task as “completed” and removes its assignment, again using a versioned write. The two manager instances coordinate solely through the shared version counters: they never exchange messages directly, and each instance retries until its write succeeds, guaranteeing that only one robot ever holds a claim on a given task at any moment. The protocol therefore requires only three shared state variables per task – the assigned robot ID, the version number, and a completion flag – making it easy to model and verify.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A pick‑task is marked completed at most once.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C2x0x5x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

CONSTANTS Robots, TaskIds

VARIABLES taskPool, completedTimes

(* --definition of the task record-- *)
TaskRecord == [assigned : Robots \cup {"none"},
               version  : Nat,
               completed: BOOLEAN]

(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ taskPool = [t \in TaskIds |-> [assigned |-> "none",
                                      version  |-> 0,
                                      completed|-> FALSE]]
    /\ completedTimes = [t \in TaskIds |-> 0]

(* Claim a task: robot reads the entry, sees it unassigned, and writes its id, bumping the version *)
Claim(r, t) ==
    /\ r \in Robots
    /\ t \in TaskIds
    /\ taskPool[t].assigned = "none"
    /\ taskPool[t].completed = FALSE
    /\ taskPool' = [taskPool EXCEPT ![t] = [assigned  |-> r,
                                            version   |-> taskPool[t].version + 1,
                                            completed |-> FALSE]]
    /\ UNCHANGED completedTimes

(* Complete a task: robot that currently holds the claim marks it completed,
   clears the assignment, bumps the version, and records the completion *)
Complete(r, t) ==
    /\ r \in Robots
    /\ t \in TaskIds
    /\ taskPool[t].assigned = r
    /\ taskPool[t].completed = FALSE
    /\ taskPool' = [taskPool EXCEPT ![t] = [assigned  |-> "none",
                                            version   |-> taskPool[t].version + 1,
                                            completed |-> TRUE]]
    /\ completedTimes' = [completedTimes EXCEPT ![t] = completedTimes[t] + 1]

(* The next-state relation: any robot may claim or complete any task, or the system may stutter *)
Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in TaskIds: Claim(r, t)
    \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in TaskIds: Complete(r, t)
    \/ UNCHANGED <<taskPool, completedTimes>>

(* Specification *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<taskPool, completedTimes>>

(* Safety invariant: a task can be marked completed at most once *)
TaskCompletedAtMostOnce == \A t \in TaskIds : completedTimes[t] <= 1

=============================================================================

nl:
The system has two participants: an Air‑Traffic Controller (ATC) process that issues landing requests and a Runway Manager process that assigns the single runway. Both processes keep a shared compare‑and‑swap register that stores a tuple (owner, token) where owner is either “none”, “ATC”, or “RM” and token is a monotonically increasing integer. When the ATC wants to schedule a plane, it reads the register; if owner is “none” it attempts a compare‑and‑swap, replacing “none” with “ATC” and incrementing the token. The Runway Manager periodically reads the same register; if it sees owner “ATC” it performs the landing, then uses compare‑and‑swap to change owner back to “none” while also bumping the token. Because network messages can be reordered, each process validates that the token it reads matches the token it expects before issuing its compare‑and‑swap, discarding stale replies if the token has changed. This way only one process can hold the “owner” field at a time, guaranteeing exclusive use of the runway despite out‑of‑order messages.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: The runway is never assigned to more than one aircraft at the same time.

nl:
The yard system has three kinds of participants: a fleet of automated cranes, a central Yard Manager that tracks which loading slots are free, and the ship’s loading plan controller that proposes which crane should work on which slot. Each crane maintains a local variable “mySlot” that is either empty or holds the identifier of the slot it believes it has reserved. The Yard Manager holds a single compare‑and‑swap register whose value is the identifier of the currently unallocated slot; a crane can issue a reservation request that atomically swaps the register’s value with the crane’s own identifier only if the register still contains the expected free‑slot identifier. After a successful swap, the crane writes the received slot identifier into its “mySlot” variable and notifies the loading‑plan controller; if the swap fails, the crane retries with the new register value. Because network messages can be reordered, a crane may receive an old “slot now free” notification after it has already moved on, but the compare‑and‑swap operation guarantees that only one crane can ever replace the register’s value for that slot. The loading‑plan controller periodically queries the Yard Manager to confirm that each slot appears in exactly one crane’s “mySlot” before issuing a “lift container” command. If a crane detects that its “mySlot” no longer matches the register (because another crane succeeded later), it releases the slot and retries with the next free slot reported by the manager.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two cranes can ever be assigned the same loading slot at the same time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C7x7x3x1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cranes, Slots      \* Finite sets of identifiers

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* State variables
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES mySlot, reg

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Helper definitions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* A special value meaning “no slot reserved”
NoSlot == "None"

\* The set of cranes that currently hold a reservation for a concrete slot
CranesWithSlot(s) == { c \in Cranes : mySlot[c] = s }

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ mySlot = [c \in Cranes |-> NoSlot]
    /\ reg \in Slots          \* the register initially points to some free slot

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* A crane attempts a compare‑and‑swap reservation.
\* The operation succeeds only if the register still contains the expected free‑slot identifier.
Reserve(c) ==
    /\ c \in Cranes
    /\ mySlot[c] = NoSlot                 \* crane is currently idle
    /\ LET expected == reg IN
       /\ expected \in Slots               \* the value we expect to be a free slot
       /\ reg' = c                         \* swap: register now holds the crane id
       /\ mySlot' = [mySlot EXCEPT ![c] = expected]  \* crane records the slot
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>                    \* no other variables change

\* A crane notices that its reservation is no longer reflected in the register
\* (e.g., because another crane later succeeded for the same slot) and releases it.
Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in Cranes
    /\ mySlot[c] # NoSlot                 \* crane believes it holds a slot
    /\ LET s == mySlot[c] IN
       /\ mySlot' = [mySlot EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]   \* forget the slot
       /\ reg' = s                                 \* make the slot free again
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>                    \* no other variables change

\* The manager may also freely set the register to any currently free slot.
ManagerAdvance ==
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
          (\A c \in Cranes : mySlot[c] # s)   \* no crane currently owns s
       /\ reg' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED mySlot

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Reserve(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Release(c)
    \/ ManagerAdvance

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety invariant: no two cranes can ever be assigned the same loading slot
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
NoDuplicateSlot ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        Cardinality(CranesWithSlot(s)) <= 1

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<mySlot, reg>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* THEOREM (for TLC) – the invariant holds
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []NoDuplicateSlot

=============================================================================

nl:
The system consists of a central Coordinator and two lock controllers, FrontDoorLock and BackDoorLock, each of which runs on a separate embedded processor. Each lock controller stores a boolean flag coarseGranted indicating whether the Coordinator has given it permission to start a fine‑grained unlock sequence, and a field fineHolder that records which user (if any) currently holds the fine lock for that door. When a user requests to unlock a door, the lock controller first sends a *coarse request* to the Coordinator; the Coordinator records the request in its own variable coarseOwner and replies with an acknowledgement, setting the controller’s coarseGranted to true. After receiving the coarse acknowledgement, the controller then sends a *fine request* specifying the user’s identity; the Coordinator checks that no other controller currently has a fine lock (its fineOwner is nil) and, if so, records the user as fineOwner and instructs the controller to complete the unlock, which it records by setting fineHolder to that user. If a lock controller crashes silently after receiving the coarse acknowledgement, it will stop responding to the fine request; the Coordinator detects the lack of a fine‑request reply within a timeout and clears its coarseOwner and fineOwner entries, allowing other doors to proceed. The protocol therefore proceeds through a two‑phase grant (coarse then fine) and uses timeout‑driven rollback to handle a silent crash. Throughout, only one controller may have its fineHolder set to a non‑nil user at any time, ensuring exclusive access to the physical unlocking mechanism.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time can two doors be physically unlocked simultaneously by different users.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C18x8x0x0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Constants
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CONSTANTS Users   \* the set of possible user identities

Door == {"FrontDoor", "BackDoor"}
NilUser == "nil"

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Variables
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES coarseGranted, fineHolder, coarseOwner, fineOwner

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Types
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CoarseGrantedType == [Door -> BOOLEAN]
FineHolderType    == [Door -> (Users \cup {NilUser})]
CoarseOwnerType   == Door \cup {NilUser}
FineOwnerType     == Users \cup {NilUser}

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ coarseGranted = [d \in Door |-> FALSE]
    /\ fineHolder    = [d \in Door |-> NilUser]
    /\ coarseOwner   = NilUser
    /\ fineOwner     = NilUser

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CoarseGrant(d) ==
    /\ d \in Door
    /\ ~coarseGranted[d]
    /\ coarseOwner'   = d
    /\ coarseGranted' = [coarseGranted EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineHolder, fineOwner >>

FineGrant(d, u) ==
    /\ d \in Door
    /\ u \in Users
    /\ coarseGranted[d]           \* door has received the coarse ack
    /\ coarseOwner = d            \* request originates from the same door
    /\ fineOwner = NilUser        \* no other fine lock held
    /\ fineOwner'   = u
    /\ fineHolder'  = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = u]
    /\ coarseGranted' = [coarseGranted EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ coarseOwner'   = NilUser
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>

Timeout(d) ==
    /\ d \in Door
    /\ coarseOwner = d
    /\ coarseGranted[d]           \* coarse grant was given
    /\ fineOwner = NilUser        \* fine request never arrived
    /\ coarseOwner'   = NilUser
    /\ coarseGranted' = [coarseGranted EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineHolder, fineOwner >>

Release(d) ==
    /\ d \in Door
    /\ fineHolder[d] # NilUser
    /\ fineHolder' = [fineHolder EXCEPT ![d] = NilUser]
    /\ fineOwner'  = NilUser
    /\ UNCHANGED << coarseGranted, coarseOwner >>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Next-state relation
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Door : CoarseGrant(d)
    \/ \E d \in Door, u \in Users : FineGrant(d, u)
    \/ \E d \in Door : Timeout(d)
    \/ \E d \in Door : Release(d)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety property (the required invariant)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* At most one door may have a non‑nil fineHolder at any time.
NoSimultaneousUnlock ==
    Cardinality({ d \in Door : fineHolder[d] # NilUser }) <= 1

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseGranted, fineHolder, coarseOwner, fineOwner>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Theorem (for TLC checking)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []NoSimultaneousUnlock

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoSimultaneousUnlock

nl:
The system consists of two load‑shedder controllers, Instance A and Instance B, each responsible for a distinct sub‑grid but both drawing from a common pool of “shed‑slots”. Each instance maintains a Boolean flag “hasCoarseLock” indicating whether it currently holds the coarse lock on the shared pool, and an integer “fineLockCount” that records how many fine‑grained shed‑slot reservations it has acquired. To begin a shedding operation, an instance first attempts to acquire the coarse lock; if the flag is false for both instances it may set its own flag to true. Once the coarse lock is held, the instance can request individual shed‑slots one at a time, incrementing its fineLockCount only after the pool reports the slot is free. When the instance has finished using a slot, it decrements fineLockCount and releases the slot back to the pool; when fineLockCount reaches zero the instance releases the coarse lock, resetting its flag. If an instance finds the coarse lock already set by the other instance, it must wait and retry, guaranteeing that at any moment only one instance can hold the coarse lock and therefore control the allocation of the shared shed‑slots.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one load‑shedder instance can hold a particular shed‑slot at any time, ensuring mutual exclusion of the shared shedding resource.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C9x8x0x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Instances, Slots, MaxSlots, None

VARIABLES hasCoarseLock, fineLockCount, slotOwner

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Type definitions to keep the state space finite                       *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ hasCoarseLock \in [Instances -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ fineLockCount \in [Instances -> 0..MaxSlots]
    /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Instances \cup {None}]

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Initial state                                                        *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Init ==
    /\ hasCoarseLock = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ fineLockCount = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ slotOwner    = [s \in Slots    |-> None]

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Actions                                                              *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* Acquire the coarse lock when nobody holds it *)
AcquireCoarse(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ ~hasCoarseLock[i]
    /\ \A j \in Instances : ~hasCoarseLock[j]
    /\ hasCoarseLock' = [hasCoarseLock EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLockCount, slotOwner>>

(* Release the coarse lock – only allowed when no fine slots are held *)
ReleaseCoarse(i) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ hasCoarseLock[i]
    /\ fineLockCount[i] = 0
    /\ hasCoarseLock' = [hasCoarseLock EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLockCount, slotOwner>>

(* Reserve a free shed‑slot while holding the coarse lock *)
AcquireSlot(i, s) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ hasCoarseLock[i]
    /\ slotOwner[s] = None
    /\ slotOwner'    = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ fineLockCount' = [fineLockCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED hasCoarseLock

(* Release a previously‑acquired slot *)
ReleaseSlot(i, s) ==
    /\ i \in Instances
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ slotOwner[s] = i
    /\ slotOwner'    = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ fineLockCount' = [fineLockCount EXCEPT ![i] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED hasCoarseLock

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Next-state relation                                                   *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances: AcquireCoarse(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: ReleaseCoarse(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: \E s \in Slots: AcquireSlot(i, s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances: \E s \in Slots: ReleaseSlot(i, s)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Specification                                                         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<hasCoarseLock, fineLockCount, slotOwner>>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Safety invariant: at most one instance holds any given slot         *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
SlotMutex ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        \A i1, i2 \in Instances :
            (slotOwner[s] = i1 /\ slotOwner[s] = i2) => i1 = i2

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Optional type invariant – also useful for TLC boundedness            *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
TypeInvariant == TypeOK

====

CONSTANTS
  Instances = {"A", "B"}
  Slots     = {1, 2}
  MaxSlots  = 2
  None      = "None"

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SlotMutex

nl:
The system consists of a fixed ring of lobby servers, each holding a local queue of waiting players, and a single privileged admin client that can intervene at any time. Each server maintains two variables: a boolean “hasToken” indicating whether it currently holds the exclusive matchmaking token, and a flag “overrideRequested” that the admin can set remotely. When a server’s hasToken is true, it may dequeue up to four players, create a match, and then pass the token clockwise to the next server in the ring. If the admin sets overrideRequested on a server, that server immediately creates a match with the first four players in its queue, regardless of whether it holds the token, and then it injects a special “override token” that skips the normal ring order and is given to the admin‑controlled server, which then passes the regular token to its successor. All other servers, upon receiving the token, first check the overrideRequested flag; if it is set they reset the flag and wait for the admin‑controlled server to hand back the token before proceeding. The admin can only issue one override at a time, and the override flag is cleared as soon as the overridden match is launched. All token transfers and flag updates are performed atomically to avoid races between servers and the admin.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A specific group of players can be placed into a match at most once.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C5x1x5x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumServers, NumPlayers, AdminServer, SpecialGroup

Servers == 1..NumServers
Players == 1..NumPlayers
N == NumServers

VARIABLES TokenHolder, OverrideRequested, queues, Matches

vars == <<TokenHolder, OverrideRequested, queues, Matches>>

(* Ring successor *)
Next(s) == IF s = N THEN 1 ELSE s + 1

(* Initial state *)
Init ==
  /\ TokenHolder = 1
  /\ OverrideRequested = {}
  /\ queues = [s \in Servers |-> {}]
  /\ Matches = {}

(* Normal operation when the holder has no override flag *)
NormalStep_NoOverride ==
  \E s \in Servers :
    /\ TokenHolder = s
    /\ s \notin OverrideRequested
    /\ \E players \in SUBSET queues[s] :
         /\ Cardinality(players) <= 4
         /\ Matches' = IF players = {} THEN Matches ELSE Matches \cup {players}
         /\ queues' = [queues EXCEPT ![s] = queues[s] \ players]
    /\ TokenHolder' = Next(s)
    /\ OverrideRequested' = OverrideRequested

(* Normal operation when the holder's override flag is set: just clear it *)
NormalStep_ClearFlag ==
  \E s \in Servers :
    /\ TokenHolder = s
    /\ s \in OverrideRequested
    /\ OverrideRequested' = {}
    /\ TokenHolder' = Next(s)

(* Admin issues an override: creates a match on a chosen server and
   transfers the regular token to the successor of the admin server. *)
OverrideAction ==
  /\ OverrideRequested = {}
  /\ \E s \in Servers :
        /\ \E players \in SUBSET queues[s] :
               /\ Cardinality(players) <= 4
               /\ Matches' = IF players = {} THEN Matches ELSE Matches \cup {players}
               /\ queues' = [queues EXCEPT ![s] = queues[s] \ players]
        /\ TokenHolder' = Next(AdminServer)
        /\ OverrideRequested' = {}

NextAction == NormalStep_NoOverride \/ NormalStep_ClearFlag \/ OverrideAction

Spec == Init /\ [][NextAction]_vars

(* Safety property: each player in SpecialGroup appears in at most one match *)
SpecialGroupAtMostOnce ==
  \A p \in SpecialGroup :
    Cardinality({ m \in Matches : p \in m }) <= 1

====================

  NumPlayers = 5
  AdminServer = 1
