The protocol involves a Settlement Manager that coordinates a single settlement batch, and two participating banks, Bank A and Bank B. Each participant keeps a local flag indicating whether it has prepared its portion of the batch, and the manager maintains a batch‑status variable that can be *open*, *coarse‑locked*, *fine‑locked*, or *committed*. To start, the manager acquires a coarse lock on the whole batch, which blocks any new batches from being opened while the current one is being processed. After the coarse lock is obtained, each bank independently requests a fine lock on its own ledger entries, prepares its debit and credit records, and sets its prepared flag. When both banks have signaled preparation, the manager upgrades the batch to the fine‑locked state, writes a commit record, and changes the batch‑status to *committed*. If either bank fails to respond within a timeout (modeling a silent crash), the manager aborts the batch, releases both coarse and fine locks, and resets the status to *open* so that the batch can be retried later. All lock acquisitions and releases are performed in a strict hierarchical order—coarse before fine and release in reverse—to avoid deadlock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A settlement batch is committed at most once.

nl:
There are two load‑shed controllers, each running an independent instance that decides when to cut power to its own set of customer segments. Both controllers compete for a single token that grants the right to issue a shed command to the shared high‑voltage breaker pool. Each controller keeps a local variable indicating whether it currently holds the token and a counter of how many shed actions it has performed since the last token hand‑off. When a controller decides a shed is needed, it first checks that it holds the token; if it does, it sends a “shed request” message to the breaker pool, receives acknowledgment, and then increments its counter. After completing a shed, the controller passes the token to the next controller in the ring by sending a “token release” message that includes its counter value. The successor controller accepts the token only if the counter in the release message matches its own expected value, preventing stale or duplicated token use. If a controller does not hold the token, it simply waits and periodically polls its neighbor for a token release, ensuring that at most one controller can command the breaker pool at any time.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No controller can issue a shed command to the shared breaker pool unless it currently holds the valid token.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C9x1x6x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* CONSTANTS
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
CONSTANTS Controllers, NoShed

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* DEFINITIONS
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* The two controllers
CONSTANT C1, C2

\* Set of controllers (must be defined in the .cfg)
\* Controllers == {C1, C2}

\* Successor function for the ring
Succ(i) == IF i = C1 THEN C2 ELSE C1

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* VARIABLES
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES holder,               \* which controller currently holds the token
          counter,              \* number of shed actions performed since last hand‑off
          lastShed              \* controller that performed the most recent shed (or NoShed)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* INITIAL STATE
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ holder \in Controllers
    /\ counter = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ lastShed = NoShed

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* ACTIONS
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Shed action for a controller i (must hold the token)
Shed(i) ==
    /\ holder = i
    /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![i] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, lastShed >>
    /\ lastShed' = i

\* Pass token from i to its successor
Pass(i) ==
    /\ holder = i
    /\ LET j == Succ(i) IN
       /\ holder' = j
       /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![i] = 0]   \* reset i's counter after hand‑off
       /\ lastShed' = NoShed                     \* clear record of last shed
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>

\* A controller that does not hold the token can simply wait (no state change)
Idle ==
    /\ UNCHANGED << holder, counter, lastShed >>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* NEXT STATE RELATION
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Controllers : Shed(i)
    \/ \E i \in Controllers : Pass(i)
    \/ Idle

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* SPECIFICATION
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holder, counter, lastShed>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* SAFETY INVARIANT
\* No controller can issue a shed command unless it currently holds the token.
\* This is captured by asserting that whenever a shed has occurred and not yet
\* been “forgotten” by a token hand‑off, the holder must be the controller that
\* performed that shed.
TokenSafety == (lastShed = NoShed) \/ (holder = lastShed)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* THEOREM (optional, for TLC)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []TokenSafety

NEXT Next
INVARIANT TokenSafety

nl:
The fleet consists of three robots—R A, R B, and R C—arranged in a logical ring order A → B → C → A. Each robot stores a single state variable “hasToken” that is true only when the token resides with it, and a second variable “inAisle” that is true while it is occupying the narrow aisle, the sole critical resource. When a robot’s “hasToken” is true it may request access to the aisle; if the aisle is free it sets “inAisle” to true, moves through, and upon completion it clears “inAisle”. After leaving the aisle the robot passes the token to its successor by setting its own “hasToken” to false and sending a token‑forward message that causes the successor’s “hasToken” to become true. If a robot is slow, it simply retains the token longer; the other robots keep their “hasToken” false and continuously poll for the token, but they never assume the token has been lost. The token‑forward message is guaranteed to be delivered, so no robot ever crashes or permanently blocks the ring, only experiences delay. The protocol thus requires only the two Boolean variables per robot and the ring topology to coordinate exclusive aisle usage.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment, no more than one robot is inside the narrow aisle.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C2x1x0x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Robots

(* ---- Variables ---- *)
VARIABLES hasToken, inAisle

(* ---- Helper definitions ---- *)
vars == <<hasToken, inAisle>>

Succ == [r \in Robots |-> 
          IF r = "A" THEN "B"
          ELSE IF r = "B" THEN "C"
          ELSE "A"]

(* ---- Initial state ---- *)
Init ==
    /\ hasToken = [r \in Robots |-> IF r = "A" THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE]
    /\ inAisle = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]

(* ---- Actions ---- *)

Enter(r) ==
    /\ r \in Robots
    /\ hasToken[r] = TRUE
    /\ inAisle[r] = FALSE
    /\ \A s \in Robots : inAisle[s] = FALSE   \* aisle is free
    /\ inAisle' = [inAisle EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED hasToken

ExitAndPass(r) ==
    /\ r \in Robots
    /\ hasToken[r] = TRUE
    /\ inAisle[r] = TRUE
    /\ inAisle' = [inAisle EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ hasToken' = [hasToken EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE,
                                   ![Succ[r]] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>

(* A robot may simply do nothing (e.g., delay) *)
Idle ==
    UNCHANGED <<hasToken, inAisle>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Enter(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : ExitAndPass(r)
    \/ Idle

(* ---- Specification (optional, not used by the cfg) ---- *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

(* ---- Safety invariant ---- *)
NoTwoInAisle ==
    \A r1, r2 \in Robots :
        (inAisle[r1] /\ inAisle[r2]) => r1 = r2

======

    Robots = {"A", "B", "C"}

NEXT Next

nl:
The system consists of three registration nodes (Node A, Node B, and Node C) that each keep a local copy of the number of seats left for a specific course and a flag indicating whether they currently hold the token. Only the node that holds the token may accept a student’s enrollment request; when it receives such a request it checks its local seats‑remaining count, decrements it if a seat is free, records the student ID, and then forwards the registration record to a central log. After processing any pending request, the token‑holder clears its own token flag and sets the token flag of its clockwise neighbour, thereby passing exclusive access around the ring. Each node also runs a watchdog timer; if a node does not see the token arrive within a preset interval, it assumes that the predecessor has crashed silently. The suspecting node then initiates a recovery phase in which it creates a new token, resets its own token flag, and notifies the remaining nodes so that the ring can continue without duplication of the token. Throughout the protocol the total number of seats for the course never changes; seats are only transferred from the “available” pool to the “registered” pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of seats, whether still available or already assigned to students, always remains equal to the original capacity of the course.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C8x1x2x0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS SeatsCap \* total capacity of the course
CONSTANTS Nodes \* {"A","B","C"}

\* Helper for clockwise neighbour
NextNode(n) == 
  CASE n = "A" -> "B"
  []  n = "B" -> "C"
  []  n = "C" -> "A"

VARIABLES seatsAvail,        \* seats still free (global truth)
          regCount,         \* number of students already registered
          tokenHolder,      \* which node currently holds the token
          seatsCopy         \* each node's local copy of seatsAvail

\*=================================================================
\* Initial state
\*=================================================================
Init ==
  /\ seatsAvail = SeatsCap
  /\ regCount   = 0
  /\ tokenHolder = "A"
  /\ seatsCopy = [n \in Nodes |-> SeatsCap]

\*=================================================================
\* Actions
\*=================================================================
\* A node that holds the token may accept a registration request
Request ==
  \E n \in Nodes :
    /\ tokenHolder = n
    /\ seatsAvail > 0               \* a seat is free
    /\ seatsAvail' = seatsAvail - 1
    /\ regCount'   = regCount + 1
    /\ tokenHolder' = NextNode(n)   \* pass the token clockwise
    /\ seatsCopy' = [seatsCopy EXCEPT 
                       ![n] = seatsCopy[n] - 1,
                       ![tokenHolder'] = seatsAvail']   \* new holder gets fresh copy
    /\ UNCHANGED << >>               \* no other variables change

\* The token can be passed without a registration (e.g., idle step)
PassToken ==
  \E n \in Nodes :
    /\ tokenHolder = n
    /\ tokenHolder' = NextNode(n)
    /\ seatsCopy' = [seatsCopy EXCEPT ![tokenHolder'] = seatsAvail]
    /\ UNCHANGED << seatsAvail, regCount >>

\* Watchdog‑triggered recovery: a node that has not seen the token creates a new one
Recovery ==
  \E n \in Nodes :
    /\ tokenHolder' = n                \* new (unique) token
    /\ seatsCopy' = [m \in Nodes |-> seatsAvail]   \* all nodes refresh their copy
    /\ UNCHANGED << seatsAvail, regCount >>

\*=================================================================
\* Next-state relation
\*=================================================================
Next == Request \/ PassToken \/ Recovery

\*=================================================================
\* Specification
\*=================================================================
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<seatsAvail, regCount, tokenHolder, seatsCopy>>

\*=================================================================
\* Safety invariant: total seats (available + already assigned) never changes
\*=================================================================
SeatsInvariant == seatsAvail + regCount = SeatsCap

\*=================================================================
\* Theorems (optional)
\*=================================================================
THEOREM Spec => []SeatsInvariant

nl:
The network consists of a set of vending machines M₁…Mₙ, each of which holds a collection of product slots and participates in a shared coordination layer.  
Every machine locally stores a *leaderID* that records which machine it believes is the current leader, and a *slotOwner* table that maps each slot to the machine assigned to restock it.  
If a machine stops receiving heartbeats from the current leader for a timeout period, it broadcasts an election request; the first machine to obtain acknowledgments from a majority becomes the new leader and updates the *leaderID* on all machines.  
The elected leader periodically issues *slotGrant* messages that assign unfilled slots to specific machines, and the recipient updates its entry in *slotOwner* accordingly.  
A privileged administrator may at any moment invoke an *adminOverride* that forces a designated machine to become the owner of a chosen slot, setting an override flag that makes all machines ignore any conflicting grant for that slot.  
Should the overridden machine fail, the leader clears the override flag and re‑assigns the slot using the normal grant process.  
All other machines simply forward election and grant messages and never change *slotOwner* for a slot whose override flag is active.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two machines ever believe they are the owner of the same product slot at the same time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C13x3x3x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

CONSTANTS Machines, Slots

VARIABLES leaderID, slotOwner, slotOwnerView, overrideFlag, overrideOwner

(*--algorithm Dummy
variables dummy = 0
end algorithm*)

(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ leaderID \in Machines
    /\ slotOwner \in [Slots -> Machines]
    /\ overrideFlag = [s \in Slots |-> FALSE]
    /\ overrideOwner = [s \in Slots |-> leaderID]   \* default owner when not overridden
    /\ slotOwnerView = [m \in Machines |-> slotOwner]

(* Election: any machine may become the leader *)
Election(m) ==
    /\ m \in Machines
    /\ leaderID' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotOwnerView, overrideFlag, overrideOwner>>

(* Leader grants a slot to a machine, only if no override flag is set *)
Grant(s, d) ==
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ d \in Machines
    /\ ~overrideFlag[s]
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ slotOwnerView' = [m \in Machines |-> [slotOwnerView[m] EXCEPT ![s] = d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaderID, overrideFlag, overrideOwner>>

(* Administrator forces an ownership override for a slot *)
AdminOverride(s, d) ==
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ d \in Machines
    /\ overrideFlag' = [overrideFlag EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ overrideOwner' = [overrideOwner EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = d]
    /\ slotOwnerView' = [m \in Machines |-> [slotOwnerView[m] EXCEPT ![s] = d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED leaderID

(* Leader clears an existing override flag (e.g., after failure) *)
ClearOverride(s) ==
    /\ s \in Slots
    /\ overrideFlag[s] = TRUE
    /\ overrideFlag' = [overrideFlag EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaderID, slotOwner, overrideOwner, slotOwnerView>>

(* The next-state relation *)
Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Election(m)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, d \in Machines : Grant(s, d)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, d \in Machines : AdminOverride(s, d)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : ClearOverride(s)

(* Full specification *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leaderID, slotOwner, slotOwnerView, overrideFlag, overrideOwner>>

(* Safety invariant: no two distinct machines both believe they own the same slot *)
NoDupOwner ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        ~\E m1, m2 \in Machines :
            /\ m1 # m2
            /\ slotOwnerView[m1][s] = m1
            /\ slotOwnerView[m2][s] = m2

nl:
The system consists of a central pharmacy server, several dispensing modules, and a capacity manager that can add or remove dispensers at runtime. Each participant keeps a tiny local copy of the shared record containing two fields: the number of pending prescriptions in the queue and the current total dispensing capacity. When a pharmacist submits a new prescription, the server proposes an increment of the queue length; each dispensing module votes on the proposal and the change is committed only after a quorum of modules acknowledges it. After a dispenser finishes a prescription, it proposes to decrement the queue length and, if it frees capacity, to update the capacity field; again a quorum must accept before the update takes effect. When the capacity manager decides to add a new dispenser or retire an existing one, it broadcasts a capacity‑change proposal that must achieve quorum before the new capacity value replaces the old one. The quorum voting rule guarantees that every action—adding a prescription, completing a dispense, or changing capacity—is applied atomically across all nodes, keeping the two‑field record consistent. Because the record has only the queue length and capacity variables, the whole protocol can be modeled with just those two state variables.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No update to the shared (queue length, capacity) record can be lost or overwritten without a quorum‑approved commit, ensuring that every prescription addition or removal is reflected exactly once.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C16x5x1x4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* State variables: the shared record consisting of a queue length and the
\* current total dispensing capacity.
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES queue, capacity

\* Upper bound on capacity for model‑checking (kept small enough for exhaustive
\* exploration).  The exact number is not important for the safety property.
CapBound == 5

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state: empty queue, a non‑zero capacity.
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ queue = 0
    /\ capacity \in 1 .. CapBound

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Actions corresponding to the three kinds of operations described.
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
AddPrescription ==
    /\ queue < capacity            \* there is free capacity
    /\ queue' = queue + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

CompleteDispense ==
    /\ queue > 0
    /\ queue' = queue - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

IncreaseCapacity ==
    /\ capacity < CapBound
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

DecreaseCapacity ==
    /\ capacity > 1
    /\ queue <= capacity - 1      \* after removal the queue still fits
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* The system can perform any of the above actions.
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ AddPrescription
    \/ CompleteDispense
    \/ IncreaseCapacity
    \/ DecreaseCapacity

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Full specification (initial condition and always‑next).
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, capacity>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety invariant: the (queue,capacity) record is always consistent.
\* No update is lost or overwritten: the queue length is never negative and
\* never exceeds the total capacity.
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
SafeRecord ==
    /\ queue >= 0
    /\ queue <= capacity

=============================================================================

nl:
The opening auction involves three kinds of participants: many traders who wish to submit orders, a single Auctioneer process that controls the order‑book slots, and a privileged Admin who can intervene at any time.  
Each price‑level slot in the order book is represented by a variable `slotOwner` that is either empty or holds the ID of the trader that currently holds the lease, and a timestamp `leaseExpiration` indicating when that lease automatically becomes void.  
When a trader wants to submit a market‑on‑close order it sends a `RequestLease` message to the Auctioneer; if `slotOwner` is empty and the current time is before `leaseExpiration`, the Auctioneer records the trader’s ID in `slotOwner` and sets `leaseExpiration` to the current time plus a fixed lease duration.  
The trader may later send a `RenewLease` before the expiry, which the Auctioneer accepts by extending `leaseExpiration`; if the lease has already expired, the trader must request a new lease.  
At any moment the Admin can issue an `AdminOverride` that sets a Boolean `adminOverrideFlag` true and immediately writes its own ID into `slotOwner`, discarding any existing lease regardless of its remaining time.  
The Auctioneer always checks `adminOverrideFlag` first; when it is true the normal lease rules are ignored until the Admin clears the flag, after which the slot becomes free again and normal traders may acquire it.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No price‑level slot can be owned simultaneously by two different traders (or by a trader and the Admin) under any circumstance.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C15x6x3x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Traders, SlotSet, LeaseDuration, MaxTime, AdminID

\* All possible participants (traders plus the privileged admin)
Participants == Traders \cup {AdminID}

\* Initial empty ownership for every slot
SlotOwnerInit == [s \in SlotSet |-> {}]

VARIABLES slotOwner, leaseExpiration, adminOverrideFlag, currentTime

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
  /\ slotOwner = SlotOwnerInit
  /\ leaseExpiration = [s \in SlotSet |-> 0]
  /\ adminOverrideFlag = FALSE
  /\ currentTime = 0

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
RequestLease(tr, s) ==
  /\ ~adminOverrideFlag
  /\ tr \in Traders
  /\ s \in SlotSet
  /\ slotOwner[s] = {}
  /\ currentTime < MaxTime
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = {tr}]
  /\ leaseExpiration' = [leaseExpiration EXCEPT ![s] =
        (currentTime + LeaseDuration) % (MaxTime + 1)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<adminOverrideFlag, currentTime>>

RenewLease(tr, s) ==
  /\ ~adminOverrideFlag
  /\ tr \in Traders
  /\ s \in SlotSet
  /\ tr \in slotOwner[s]
  /\ currentTime < leaseExpiration[s]
  /\ leaseExpiration' = [leaseExpiration EXCEPT ![s] =
        (currentTime + LeaseDuration) % (MaxTime + 1)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, adminOverrideFlag, currentTime>>

ExpireLease(s) ==
  /\ ~adminOverrideFlag
  /\ s \in SlotSet
  /\ slotOwner[s] # {}
  /\ currentTime >= leaseExpiration[s]
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ leaseExpiration' = [leaseExpiration EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<adminOverrideFlag, currentTime>>

AdminOverride(s) ==
  /\ ~adminOverrideFlag
  /\ s \in SlotSet
  /\ adminOverrideFlag' = TRUE
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = {AdminID}]
  /\ leaseExpiration' = [leaseExpiration EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED currentTime

ClearAdmin(s) ==
  /\ adminOverrideFlag
  /\ s \in SlotSet
  /\ adminOverrideFlag' = FALSE
  /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ leaseExpiration' = [leaseExpiration EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED currentTime

Tick ==
  /\ currentTime < MaxTime
  /\ currentTime' = currentTime + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, leaseExpiration, adminOverrideFlag>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
  \/ \E s \in SlotSet, tr \in Traders: RequestLease(tr, s)
  \/ \E s \in SlotSet, tr \in Traders: RenewLease(tr, s)
  \/ \E s \in SlotSet: ExpireLease(s)
  \/ \E s \in SlotSet: AdminOverride(s)
  \/ \E s \in SlotSet: ClearAdmin(s)
  \/ Tick

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety invariant: a slot never has more than one owner (no two traders,
\* and never a trader together with the admin)
NoDoubleOwner ==
  \A s \in SlotSet: Cardinality(slotOwner[s]) <= 1

====

INIT Init

nl:
The system consists of a central coordinator (the reservation service) and a set of branch libraries that each hold copies of a particular book.  
Each branch maintains a single state variable for that book: either “available” or “tentatively reserved”.  
When a patron requests a reservation, the coordinator sends a prepare request to all branches that have a copy of the book.  
Each branch that still has the book “available” records “tentatively reserved” and replies “agree”; if the book is already locked it replies “reject”.  
The coordinator waits for all replies, but if a branch is slow it continues to wait up to a configurable grace period; after the period, if no reject has been received, the coordinator sends a commit message, otherwise it sends an abort.  
Upon receiving commit, a branch changes its state to “reserved permanently”; upon abort it restores the state to “available”.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of reserved copies of the book never exceeds the total number of physical copies owned by all branches.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C19x2x2x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Branch

VARIABLES branchState, pending, pendingTentative, rejectSeen

\* Number of physical copies owned by all branches
NumCopies == Cardinality(Branch)

\* Initial state: every branch has the book available, no transaction in progress
Init ==
    /\ branchState = [b \in Branch |-> "available"]
    /\ pending = FALSE
    /\ pendingTentative = {}
    /\ rejectSeen = FALSE

\* Coordinator initiates a reservation request
Request ==
    /\ ~pending
    /\ pending' = TRUE
    /\ pendingTentative' = {}
    /\ rejectSeen' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED branchState

\* A single branch responds to the prepare request
BranchRespond(b) ==
    /\ pending
    /\ b \in Branch
    /\ b \notin pendingTentative
    /\ IF branchState[b] = "available"
          THEN /\ branchState' = [branchState EXCEPT ![b] = "tentative"]
               /\ pendingTentative' = pendingTentative \cup {b}
               /\ rejectSeen' = rejectSeen
          ELSE /\ branchState' = branchState
               /\ pendingTentative' = pendingTentative
               /\ rejectSeen' = TRUE
    /\ pending' = pending

\* Coordinator decides to commit (no reject was seen)
Commit ==
    /\ pending
    /\ ~rejectSeen
    /\ branchState' = [b \in Branch |-> IF b \in pendingTentative THEN "reserved" ELSE branchState[b]]
    /\ pending' = FALSE
    /\ pendingTentative' = {}
    /\ rejectSeen' = FALSE

\* Coordinator decides to abort (at least one reject was seen)
Abort ==
    /\ pending
    /\ rejectSeen
    /\ branchState' = [b \in Branch |-> IF b \in pendingTentative THEN "available" ELSE branchState[b]]
    /\ pending' = FALSE
    /\ pendingTentative' = {}
    /\ rejectSeen' = FALSE

Next ==
    \/ Request
    \/ \E b \in Branch : BranchRespond(b)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort

vars == <<branchState, pending, pendingTentative, rejectSeen>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety invariant: the number of permanently reserved copies never exceeds the total number of copies
SafeReserved ==
    Cardinality({b \in Branch : branchState[b] = "reserved"}) <= NumCopies

nl:
The system has three kinds of participants: players, a lobby server, and a matchmaker process. Each player maintains a local variable “desiredGameMode” and a boolean “joined”. The lobby server holds a single compare‑and‑swap register that stores the identifier of the current pending match (or empty). When a player wants to join, it sends a “join request” message to the lobby server; the server reads the register, and if it is empty it attempts a compare‑and‑swap from empty to the player’s identifier, thereby claiming the spot for a new match. If the compare‑and‑swap succeeds, the server records the player as the first member of the match and broadcasts a “match‑started” message; if it fails because another player already claimed the spot, the server adds the player to a waiting list and later includes them when the match fills. Because network messages may arrive out of order, the server tags each reply with a monotonically increasing version number and ignores any stale “join request” that carries a version lower than the current register value. Players only set their local “joined” flag when they receive a “match‑started” message that references the same version they sent, ensuring consistency despite reordering.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of players recorded by the lobby server as belonging to a match never exceeds the number of distinct join requests it has received, so no player is created or duplicated.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C5x7x2x1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Player          \* Set of player identifiers

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Constants
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Empty == "empty"          \* value that denotes an empty CAS register

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Variables
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES
    reg,          \* compare‑and‑swap register (either Empty or a Player)
    regVer,       \* monotonically increasing version number of the register
    waiting,      \* set of players that have sent a join request but are waiting
    matchMembers, \* set of players that the lobby server records as belonging to the current match
    joinRequests, \* set of distinct join requests that have been received
    joined        \* [Player -> BOOLEAN] flag indicating whether each player has set its local “joined”

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Type correctness
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Player \/ reg = Empty
    /\ regVer \in Nat
    /\ waiting \subseteq Player
    /\ matchMembers \subseteq Player
    /\ joinRequests \subseteq Player
    /\ joined \in [Player -> BOOLEAN]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ reg = Empty
    /\ regVer = 0
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ matchMembers = {}
    /\ joinRequests = {}
    /\ joined = [p \in Player |-> FALSE]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* A player p sends a join request; the server processes it immediately.
Join(p) ==
    /\ p \in Player
    /\ p \notin joinRequests
    /\ joinRequests' = joinRequests \cup {p}
    /\ IF reg = Empty THEN
          /\ reg' = p
          /\ regVer' = regVer + 1
          /\ matchMembers' = matchMembers \cup {p}
          /\ waiting' = waiting
       ELSE
          /\ reg' = reg
          /\ regVer' = regVer
          /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {p}
          /\ matchMembers' = matchMembers
    /\ UNCHANGED <<joined>>

\* When the match is considered “full” the server moves all waiting players
\* into the match record.
FillMatch ==
    /\ matchMembers' = matchMembers \cup waiting
    /\ waiting' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, regVer, joinRequests, joined>>

\* A player p sets its local joined flag after receiving a matching
\* “match‑started” message.
PlayerJoined(p) ==
    /\ p \in Player
    /\ p \in matchMembers
    /\ joined' = [joined EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, regVer, waiting, joinRequests, matchMembers>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Player: Join(p)
    \/ FillMatch
    \/ \E p \in Player: PlayerJoined(p)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, regVer, waiting, matchMembers, joinRequests, joined>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety property (non‑trivial invariant)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
SafetyInv ==
    Cardinality(matchMembers) <= Cardinality(joinRequests)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Theorems (optional)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []SafetyInv

====

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SafetyInv

nl:
The system consists of a central scheduler and several robot agents that need to jointly reserve a high‑capacity pallet lift for moving a batch of crates. Each robot keeps a local flag “vote” that can be either “yes” (ready to use the lift) or “null” (not yet voted), and the scheduler maintains a counter of how many “yes” votes have been received. When a batch of crates is ready, the scheduler initiates a two‑phase commit by broadcasting a “prepare” request to all robots that could be involved. Upon receiving the prepare request, each robot checks its own task queue; if it can pause its current job, it sets its vote to “yes” and replies, otherwise it replies “no”. The scheduler waits until it has either collected a “yes” from every required robot or until a timeout expires; a slow robot may delay its reply but the scheduler does not consider it failed. If all required robots responded “yes” before the timeout, the scheduler sends a “commit” message telling them to move to the lift, and each robot changes its state to “using lift”. If any robot responded “no” or the timeout elapsed, the scheduler sends an “abort” message, all robots clear their vote flag, and the lift remains idle.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment, at most one robot may be positioned on the pallet lift.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4C2x2x0x3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots

VARIABLES vote, state, phase, counter, timeout

(* --algorithm placeholder for readability -- *)

Init ==
    /\ vote   = [r \in Robots |-> "null"]
    /\ state  = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
    /\ phase  = "idle"
    /\ counter = 0
    /\ timeout = FALSE

Prepare ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "waiting"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, state, counter, timeout>>

RobotVoteYes(r) ==
    /\ phase = "waiting"
    /\ vote[r] = "null"
    /\ vote'   = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = "yes"]
    /\ counter' = counter + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, phase, timeout>>

RobotVoteNo(r) ==
    /\ phase = "waiting"
    /\ vote[r] = "null"
    /\ vote'   = [vote EXCEPT ![r] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, phase, counter, timeout>>

TimeoutOccur ==
    /\ phase = "waiting"
    /\ ~timeout
    /\ timeout' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, state, counter, phase>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "waiting"
    /\ \A r \in Robots : vote[r] # "no"
    /\ \A r \in Robots : vote[r] = "yes" \/ vote[r] = "null"
    /\ \E r \in Robots : vote[r] = "yes"
    /\ LET YesSet == { r \in Robots : vote[r] = "yes" } IN
         /\ counter = Cardinality(YesSet)
         /\ LET chosen == CHOOSE r \in YesSet : TRUE IN
                state' = [state EXCEPT ![chosen] = "usingLift"]
    /\ vote'   = [r \in Robots |-> "null"]
    /\ counter' = 0
    /\ phase'   = "committed"
    /\ timeout' = FALSE

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "waiting"
    /\ ( \E r \in Robots : vote[r] = "no" ) \/ timeout
    /\ vote'   = [r \in Robots |-> "null"]
    /\ counter' = 0
    /\ phase'   = "aborted"
    /\ timeout' = FALSE
    /\ state'   = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]

Release ==
    /\ phase = "committed"
    /\ \E r \in Robots : state[r] = "usingLift"
    /\ LET r == CHOOSE r \in Robots : state[r] = "usingLift" IN
           state' = [state EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, phase, counter, timeout>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase \in {"aborted","committed"}
    /\ \A r \in Robots : state[r] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, state, counter, timeout>>

Next ==
    \/ Prepare
    \/ \E r \in Robots : RobotVoteYes(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : RobotVoteNo(r)
    \/ TimeoutOccur
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Release
    \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<vote, state, phase, counter, timeout>>

(* Safety invariant: at most one robot is on the pallet lift *)
LiftSafety == Cardinality({ r \in Robots : state[r] = "usingLift" }) <= 1

=============================================================================

INIT Init

nl:
The system consists of two independent wash lines, Line A and Line B, each controlled by a line controller that schedules cars onto its conveyor and requests the shared cleaning‑solution pump. Each line maintains a small local state: the number of cars currently on its conveyor (0 or 1) and a version number that records the last observed state of the pump. When a car reaches the wash bay, the line controller reads the pump’s current version; if the pump is free it writes a new version to claim it, otherwise it aborts and retries after a brief back‑off. If the write succeeds, the controller marks the pump as occupied and starts the wash cycle; when the cycle finishes the controller releases the pump by resetting its version. If the write fails because another line updated the version in the meantime, the controller retries the whole acquisition step, leaving its conveyor unchanged. Both controllers run concurrently but never block each other; they only communicate through the shared pump’s version field, which provides optimistic locking with automatic retries. The protocol therefore needs only three state variables in total: the pump version, the pump‑occupied flag, and the per‑line conveyor count.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cleaning‑solution pump is never allocated to more than one car at the same time.
spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4C4x0x4x2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANTS Lines

VARIABLES pumpVersion, pumpOccupied, conveyor, lineVersion

(* --algorithm definition omitted; using actions directly *)

Init ==
    /\ pumpVersion = 0
    /\ pumpOccupied = FALSE
    /\ conveyor   = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ lineVersion = [l \in Lines |-> 0]

CarArrives(l) ==
    /\ l \in Lines
    /\ conveyor[l] = 0
    /\ conveyor' = [conveyor EXCEPT ![l] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pumpVersion, pumpOccupied, lineVersion>>

Acquire(l) ==
    /\ l \in Lines
    /\ conveyor[l] = 1
    /\ IF ~pumpOccupied
          THEN
              LET newV == pumpVersion + 1 IN
                  /\ pumpOccupied' = TRUE
                  /\ pumpVersion'   = newV
                  /\ lineVersion'   = [lineVersion EXCEPT ![l] = newV]
          ELSE
              /\ UNCHANGED <<pumpVersion, pumpOccupied, lineVersion, conveyor>>
    /\ UNCHANGED conveyor

WashComplete(l) ==
    /\ l \in Lines
    /\ pumpOccupied = TRUE
    /\ lineVersion[l] = pumpVersion
    /\ pumpOccupied' = FALSE
    /\ pumpVersion'   = 0
    /\ conveyor'     = [conveyor EXCEPT ![l] = 0]
    /\ lineVersion'  = [lineVersion EXCEPT ![l] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Lines: CarArrives(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lines: Acquire(l)
    \/ \E l \in Lines: WashComplete(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<pumpVersion, pumpOccupied, conveyor, lineVersion>>

(* Safety invariant: the pump is never allocated to more than one car *)
PumpSafety ==
    ~(\E l1, l2 \in Lines :
          /\ l1 # l2
          /\ pumpOccupied
          /\ lineVersion[l1] = pumpVersion
          /\ lineVersion[l2] = pumpVersion)

The fleet consists of autonomous robots that move pallets and a shared compare‑and‑swap (CAS) register representing a loading bay. Each robot keeps a local copy of two variables: the identifier of the robot that currently owns the bay (or “none”) and the number of pallets already placed in the bay. To start loading, a robot reads the register; if the owner field is “none” it issues a CAS operation that tries to replace “none” with its own identifier, leaving the pallet count unchanged. If the CAS succeeds the robot becomes the exclusive owner, loads pallets one by one while incrementing the local count, and finally writes a release entry that sets the owner back to “none” and resets the count to zero. Because messages may be reordered, a robot may see an outdated owner value, but the atomic CAS guarantees that only the first robot whose CAS succeeds actually changes the register. Robots that lose the CAS simply retry later, preserving the invariant that at most one robot believes it owns the bay at any time. The protocol therefore requires only the two state variables (owner and count) to capture all relevant information.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of pallets in any loading bay never exceeds its maximum capacity.

nl:
The system consists of three participants: a LoadController that decides when to reduce demand, a group of Substation agents that own individual feeder circuits, and a privileged Admin that can intervene in emergencies. Each Substation maintains a coarse‑grained “grid lock” flag indicating whether any load‑shedding operation is in progress, and a fine‑grained “feeder lock” flag for its own circuit. When the LoadController wants to shed load, it first sets the grid lock; only after the grid lock is observed as set do the Substations each try to acquire their feeder lock, and a Substation that succeeds will open its circuit breaker to drop load. After the breaker is opened, the Substation clears its feeder lock, and when all feeders have responded the LoadController releases the grid lock. The Admin override can be invoked at any time: the Admin acquires the grid lock (or waits until it is free), sets an “override” flag, and then forces a specific Substation to open its breaker without needing that Substation’s feeder lock. The protocol guarantees that once a breaker has been opened for a particular load‑shedding request, no other participant will attempt to open it again for the same request.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A feeder’s circuit breaker is opened at most once for any single load‑shedding activation.

---- MODULE W4C9x8x5x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

CONSTANTS Substations

VARIABLES gridLock, feederLocks, breakerOpen, openCount, overrideFlag

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  Initialization
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
Init ==
  /\ gridLock = FALSE
  /\ feederLocks = [s \in Substations |-> FALSE]
  /\ breakerOpen = [s \in Substations |-> FALSE]
  /\ openCount   = [s \in Substations |-> 0]
  /\ overrideFlag = FALSE

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  LoadController actions
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
StartLoadShedding ==
  /\ ~gridLock
  /\ gridLock' = TRUE
  /\ openCount' = [s \in Substations |-> 0]
  /\ breakerOpen' = [s \in Substations |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feederLocks, overrideFlag>>

ReleaseGridLock ==
  /\ gridLock
  /\ gridLock' = FALSE
  /\ overrideFlag' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feederLocks, breakerOpen, openCount>>

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  Substation actions
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
AcquireFeederLock(s) ==
  /\ gridLock
  /\ s \in Substations
  /\ feederLocks[s] = FALSE
  /\ feederLocks' = [feederLocks EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridLock, breakerOpen, openCount, overrideFlag>>

OpenBreaker(s) ==
  /\ gridLock
  /\ s \in Substations
  /\ feederLocks[s] = TRUE
  /\ openCount[s] = 0               \* not opened yet for this request
  /\ breakerOpen' = [breakerOpen EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ feederLocks' = [feederLocks EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ openCount'   = [openCount EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gridLock, overrideFlag>>

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  Admin actions (override)
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
AdminForceOpen(s) ==
  /\ ~gridLock
  /\ s \in Substations
  /\ openCount[s] = 0               \* must not have opened yet for this request
  /\ gridLock'     = TRUE
  /\ overrideFlag' = TRUE
  /\ breakerOpen'  = [breakerOpen EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
  /\ openCount'    = [openCount EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED feederLocks

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  Next-state relation
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
Next ==
  \/ StartLoadShedding
  \/ ReleaseGridLock
  \/ \E s \in Substations: AcquireFeederLock(s)
  \/ \E s \in Substations: OpenBreaker(s)
  \/ \E s \in Substations: AdminForceOpen(s)

\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
\*  Safety invariant: a feeder’s breaker is opened at most once per request
\*---------------------------------------------------------------------- 
NoDoubleOpen == \A s \in Substations : openCount[s] <= 1

=============================================================================

nl:
The system consists of three autonomous routing agents – the Sorter, the Diverter, and the Loader – each of which needs temporary exclusive control of a shared conveyor segment called the “routing slot”. All agents read and write a single compare‑and‑swap register that stores the identifier of the agent that currently owns the routing slot, or the special value FREE. When an agent wants to use the slot it reads the register; if the value is FREE it attempts a compare‑and‑swap from FREE to its own identifier, succeeding only if no other agent has changed the value in the meantime. The privileged administrator runs a separate Override process that can atomically replace any register value with the identifier ADMIN, thereby pre‑empting the current holder and taking control of the slot for emergency re‑routing. After the admin finishes, it writes the register back to FREE, allowing the normal agents to compete again. Any agent that loses a compare‑and‑swap attempt simply retries after a short back‑off, while the admin’s override operation never retries – it succeeds immediately. The protocol therefore requires only two state variables – the register’s current owner and a Boolean “override active” flag – to capture all possible configurations.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment, at most one routing agent or the administrator can hold the routing slot.

---------------------------- MODULE W4C17x7x0x5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Agents, ADMIN, FREE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* State variables *)
VARIABLES reg, OverrideActive

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Helper definitions *)
IsAgent(a) == a \in Agents

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ reg = FREE
    /\ OverrideActive = FALSE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Agent actions: try to acquire the slot when it is FREE and no
   override is active. *)
AgentTry(a) ==
    /\ IsAgent(a)
    /\ ~OverrideActive
    /\ reg = FREE
    /\ reg' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED OverrideActive

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Administrator actions *)
AdminOverride ==
    /\ ~OverrideActive
    /\ reg' = ADMIN
    /\ OverrideActive' = TRUE

AdminRelease ==
    /\ OverrideActive
    /\ reg = ADMIN
    /\ reg' = FREE
    /\ OverrideActive' = FALSE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Stuttering step to avoid deadlock *)
Stutter ==
    UNCHANGED <<reg, OverrideActive>>

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Next-state relation *)
Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Agents: AgentTry(a)
    \/ AdminOverride
    \/ AdminRelease
    \/ Stutter

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Specification *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, OverrideActive>>

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
(* Safety invariant: at most one holder of the routing slot *)
SlotExclusive ==
    /\ (reg = ADMIN)      => OverrideActive = TRUE
    /\ OverrideActive     => reg = ADMIN
    /\ (reg \in Agents)   => OverrideActive = FALSE
    /\ (reg = FREE)       => OverrideActive = FALSE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------------*)
THEOREM Spec => []SlotExclusive

=============================================================================

nl:
The system consists of a set of student agents that each try to enroll in a particular course, and a single course manager that holds a compare‑and‑swap register representing the number of seats still available. The register stores the current seat count and a version tag that changes only when a successful compare‑and‑swap is performed. When a student wishes to register, it first reads the current seat count and version, decides that it can enroll only if at least one seat is reported, and then issues a compare‑and‑swap that attempts to replace the old pair (count, version) with a new pair where the count is reduced by one and the version is incremented. If the compare‑and‑swap succeeds, the student knows its enrollment is confirmed; if it fails, the student repeats the read‑modify‑write loop using the newly observed values. Because a student may be slow, it might take several attempts before its compare‑and‑swap finally succeeds, but the register never loses updates from other participants. The course manager never aborts the registration process; it only ever decrements the seat count when a compare‑and‑swap succeeds, guaranteeing that the count never goes below zero. All participants eventually observe a stable seat count that reflects exactly the number of confirmed enrollments.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A seat is removed from the course’s available count at most once for each successful enrollment.

------------------------------- MODULE W4C8x7x5x3 -------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS
    Students, \* a non‑empty finite set of student identifiers
    Seats      \* the initial number of seats (Nat)

VARIABLES
    reg,      \* the compare‑and‑swap register: a record with fields count, ver
    obs,      \* each student’s last observed pair (count,ver)
    Enrolled  \* set of students that have already succeeded

(* ---------------------------- Types ----------------------------------- *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [count: Nat, ver: Nat]
    /\ obs \in [Students -> [c: Nat, v: Nat]]
    /\ Enrolled \subseteq Students

(* --------------------------- Init ------------------------------------ *)
Init ==
    /\ reg = [count |-> Seats, ver |-> 0]
    /\ obs = [s \in Students |-> [c |-> Seats, v |-> 0]]
    /\ Enrolled = {}

(* -------------------------- Actions --------------------------------- *)

\* A student reads the current register value.
Read(s) ==
    /\ s \in Students \ Enrolled
    /\ obs' = [obs EXCEPT ![s] = [c |-> reg.count, v |-> reg.ver]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, Enrolled>>

\* A student attempts a compare‑and‑swap using its last observed values.
CAS(s) ==
    /\ s \in Students \ Enrolled
    /\ obs[s].c >= 1                         \* student believes a seat is available
    /\ IF reg = [count |-> obs[s].c, ver |-> obs[s].v]
          THEN /\ reg' = [count |-> reg.count - 1,
                         ver   |-> reg.ver + 1]
               /\ Enrolled' = Enrolled \cup {s}
               /\ UNCHANGED obs
          ELSE /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, Enrolled, obs>>

(* --------------------------- Next ------------------------------------ *)
Next ==
    \E s \in Students \ Enrolled:
        \/ Read(s)
        \/ CAS(s)

(* --------------------------- Spec ------------------------------------ *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, obs, Enrolled>>

(* --------------------------- Invariant ------------------------------ *)
\* Safety: each decrement of the seat count corresponds to exactly one
\* distinct successful enrollment.
SeatsRemovedOnce ==
    Seats - reg.count = Cardinality(Enrolled)

=============================================================================

The system consists of a central coordinator and a set of local load‑shed controllers (LSCs) that each control a set of curtailable loads. Each LSC keeps a small record of the most recent “slot request” it sent and whether a “slot grant” has been received for the current shedding instance. When a shedding event is detected, the coordinator starts a two‑phase commit for that instance: it first broadcasts a **prepare** message listing the pool of time slots that may be used, and each LSC replies with a **vote** indicating which slot it would like to occupy. After collecting all votes, the coordinator selects a unique slot for each LSC, ensuring that the same slot is not assigned to two LSCs, and then sends a **commit** message that includes the chosen slot for the instance. Upon receiving the commit, an LSC records the slot as “committed” and begins shedding its load at the appointed time. A second, independent shedding instance may start while the first is still in progress, but both instances draw from the same shared pool of slots; the coordinator therefore runs two parallel two‑phase commits, each using the same state variables (requested slot, committed slot) but distinguished by an instance identifier. The protocol guarantees that even with overlapping instances, each slot is granted to at most one LSC in a given instance.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No time slot in the shared pool is allocated to more than one load‑shed controller for the same shedding instance.

---------------------------- MODULE W4C9x2x3x2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS LSCs, Slots, Instances

VARIABLES active, requested, committed

(* --algorithm description
   active[inst] ∈ BOOLEAN                     \* true iff instance inst is in progress
   requested[inst][l] ∈ Slots ∪ {None}        \* slot that LSC l has requested for inst
   committed[inst][l] ∈ Slots ∪ {None}        \* slot finally granted to LSC l for inst
*)

\* ---------- Helper definitions ----------
None == "None"

\* the set of all variable values (used for stuttering)
vars == << active, requested, committed >>

\* No two different LSCs are assigned the same non‑None slot in the given mapping.
NoDup(map) ==
  \A l1, l2 \in LSCs :
    ( map[l1] # None /\ map[l2] # None /\ map[l1] = map[l2] ) => l1 = l2

\* ---------- Initial state ----------
Init ==
  /\ active = [inst \in Instances |-> FALSE]
  /\ requested = [inst \in Instances |-> [l \in LSCs |-> None]]
  /\ committed = [inst \in Instances |-> [l \in LSCs |-> None]]

\* ---------- Actions ----------
Start(inst) ==
  /\ ~active[inst]
  /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![inst] = TRUE]
  /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![inst] = [l \in LSCs |-> None]]
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![inst] = [l \in LSCs |-> None]]
  /\ UNCHANGED << >>

Vote(inst, l, s) ==
  /\ active[inst]
  /\ requested[inst][l] = None
  /\ s \in Slots
  /\ requested' = [requested EXCEPT ![inst][l] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED << active, committed >>

Commit(inst) ==
  /\ active[inst]
  /\ \A l \in LSCs : requested[inst][l] # None      \* every LSC has voted
  /\ NoDup(requested[inst])                         \* coordinator guarantees distinct slots
  /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![inst] = requested[inst]]
  /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![inst] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED requested

\* Stuttering step to avoid deadlock
Stutter ==
  UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E inst \in Instances : Start(inst)
  \/ \E inst \in Instances, l \in LSCs, s \in Slots : Vote(inst, l, s)
  \/ \E inst \in Instances : Commit(inst)
  \/ Stutter

\* ---------- Safety invariant ----------
SafetyInv ==
  \A inst \in Instances : NoDup(committed[inst])

\* ---------- Specification ----------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

=============================================================================

nl:
The lobby server keeps a single epoch counter that is increased each time a new match is formed or the player set changes. Every player stores locally the epoch number it most recently heard from the server together with the list of players that belong to that epoch’s lobby. When a player wants to join a match it sends a join request to the server, the server records the request, increments the epoch, and broadcasts the new epoch and updated player list to all participants. A player that receives a broadcast adopts the new epoch and replaces its local lobby list, but if it is slow it may continue to operate with an older epoch until the next broadcast arrives. When the server decides the lobby is full for the current epoch it sends a “start match” message tagged with that epoch; players only start the game if the epoch on the start message matches the epoch they have stored. If a slow player later receives a newer epoch broadcast, it discards any pending start messages from older epochs and synchronizes to the current lobby configuration before proceeding. The server never includes more player identifiers in a lobby than the configured maximum, and all participants agree on the same epoch before any match begins.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time does any lobby contain more players than its configured capacity.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C5x9x4x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS MaxCapacity, MaxPlayers

(* The set of all possible player identifiers *)
Players == 1 .. MaxPlayers

VARIABLES epoch, lobby, playerEpoch, playerLobby

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Initial state *)
Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ lobby = {}
    /\ playerEpoch = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ playerLobby = [p \in Players |-> {}]

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Server actions *)

(* A player p requests to join; the server adds p if capacity allows *)
Join(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ p \notin lobby
    /\ Cardinality(lobby) < MaxCapacity
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ lobby' = lobby \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED << playerEpoch, playerLobby >>

(* The server broadcasts the current epoch and lobby to all players *)
Broadcast ==
    /\ epoch' = epoch
    /\ lobby' = lobby
    /\ playerEpoch' = [p \in Players |-> epoch]
    /\ playerLobby' = [p \in Players |-> lobby]

(* The server decides the lobby is full and sends a start‑match message *)
StartMatch ==
    /\ epoch' = epoch
    /\ lobby' = lobby
    /\ UNCHANGED << playerEpoch, playerLobby >>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Player actions *)

(* A (possibly slow) player p receives the latest broadcast *)
ReceiveBroadcast(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ playerEpoch' = [playerEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ playerLobby' = [playerLobby EXCEPT ![p] = lobby]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, lobby >>

(* Player p receives a start‑match message; it starts only if epochs match *)
ReceiveStart(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ playerEpoch[p] = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, lobby, playerEpoch, playerLobby >>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Next-state relation *)

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : Join(p)
    \/ Broadcast
    \/ StartMatch
    \/ \E p \in Players : ReceiveBroadcast(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players : ReceiveStart(p)

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Specification *)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, lobby, playerEpoch, playerLobby>>

(* ------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* Safety invariant: the lobby never exceeds its configured capacity *)

CapacityInvariant == Cardinality(lobby) <= MaxCapacity

====

nl:
The system has three participants: a **RouterController** that decides which conveyor slot a piece of baggage should take, a set of **ConveyorSegments** each representing a physical slot on the belt, and **SorterWorkers** that physically move the baggage into the chosen slot. Each participant keeps a tiny amount of state: a Boolean *coarseLock* indicating whether the controller is currently deciding a destination, a Boolean *fineLock[slot]* for each slot showing whether that slot is being claimed, and a variable *allocated[slot]* that records which baggage (if any) is currently assigned to the slot. When a SorterWorker receives a new bag, it first requests the RouterController to acquire the *coarseLock*; once granted, the controller selects an empty slot and asks the worker to acquire the corresponding *fineLock[slot]* before writing the bag’s identifier into *allocated[slot]*. After the assignment, the worker releases the *fineLock[slot]* and the controller releases the *coarseLock*, allowing other decisions to proceed. If a SorterWorker crashes silently while holding a fine lock, a watchdog timeout on the controller detects the missing heartbeat, forces the release of that *fineLock[slot]*, and clears *allocated[slot]* so the slot can be reused. All participants respect the lock hierarchy, never acquiring a fine lock without first holding the coarse lock, which keeps the protocol simple enough to be captured with only the three state variables described.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two bags are ever assigned to the same conveyor slot at the same time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C17x8x3x0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANTS Slots, Bags

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   State variables
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
VARIABLES
    coarseLock,          \* Boolean: true when controller holds the coarse lock
    fineLock,            \* Function [Slots -> BOOLEAN]: fine lock per slot
    allocated            \* Function [Slots -> Bags \cup {"NULL"}]: bag assigned or NULL

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Constants
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
NULL == "NULL"

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Initial state
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = FALSE
    /\ fineLock = [s \in Slots |-> FALSE]
    /\ allocated = [s \in Slots |-> NULL]

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Actions
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* A SorterWorker asks the controller for the coarse lock *)
AcquireCoarse ==
    /\ ~coarseLock
    /\ coarseLock' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineLock, allocated >>

(* Controller selects an empty slot for a bag and the worker acquires the
   corresponding fine lock before writing the bag identifier *)
ChooseSlot(bag, slot) ==
    /\ coarseLock = TRUE
    /\ ~fineLock[slot]
    /\ allocated[slot] = NULL
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![slot] = TRUE]
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![slot] = bag]
    /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

(* After the bag has been placed, the worker releases the fine lock and
   clears the slot *)
ReleaseFine(slot) ==
    /\ fineLock[slot] = TRUE
    /\ allocated[slot] # NULL
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![slot] = FALSE]
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![slot] = NULL]
    /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

(* Controller releases the coarse lock, allowing other decisions *)
ReleaseCoarse ==
    /\ coarseLock = TRUE
    /\ coarseLock' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED << fineLock, allocated >>

(* Watchdog: if a worker crashes while holding a fine lock, the controller
   clears the lock and the allocation *)
WatchdogRelease(slot) ==
    /\ fineLock[slot] = TRUE
    /\ allocated[slot] # NULL
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![slot] = FALSE]
    /\ allocated' = [allocated EXCEPT ![slot] = NULL]
    /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Next-state relation
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Next ==
    \/ AcquireCoarse
    \/ \E bag \in Bags: \E slot \in Slots: ChooseSlot(bag, slot)
    \/ \E slot \in Slots: ReleaseFine(slot)
    \/ ReleaseCoarse
    \/ \E slot \in Slots: WatchdogRelease(slot)

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Safety invariant: no two bags are ever assigned to the same conveyor
   slot at the same time.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
NoTwoBagsSameSlot ==
    \A s \in Slots :
        \A b1, b2 \in Bags :
            (allocated[s] = b1 /\ allocated[s] = b2) => b1 = b2

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Specification
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, fineLock, allocated>>

=============================================================================

nl:
The system consists of multiple aircraft that need a runway and a single tower process that owns a compare‑and‑swap register representing the current runway assignment.  
Each aircraft keeps a local variable “mySlot” that is either “none” or the identifier of the runway it believes it has been granted.  
When an aircraft wants to land it sends a REQUEST message containing its identifier to the tower and then reads the register; if the register is empty it attempts a compare‑and‑swap that changes the register from empty to its own identifier.  
The tower, upon receiving a REQUEST, may send a GRANT message with the current register content, but because the network can reorder messages the aircraft may see the GRANT before its own compare‑and‑swap succeeds.  
After a successful compare‑and‑swap the aircraft records the runway identifier in mySlot and proceeds to land; if the compare‑and‑swap fails it discards any earlier GRANT and retries with a new REQUEST.  
When the aircraft finishes using the runway it sends a RELEASE message and performs a compare‑and‑swap that changes the register from its identifier back to empty, guaranteeing that only one aircraft can hold the runway at a time even if RELEASE arrives out of order.  
The tower never writes directly to the register; all changes are mediated by the aircraft’s compare‑and‑swap operations, so the register’s value always reflects the single runway holder.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At any moment at most one aircraft holds the runway, i.e., the runway is never assigned to two aircraft simultaneously.

nl:
The scheduler consists of a central Coordinator and two participant services: the Surgeon service that holds the surgeon’s availability and the Room service that holds the operating‑room calendar.  
Each participant keeps a single flag indicating whether it has “prepared” a tentative booking for a requested surgery time slot.  
When a new surgery request arrives, the Coordinator sends a “prepare” message to both participants asking them to reserve the requested slot temporarily.  
Upon receiving a prepare request, a participant checks its own calendar; if the slot is free it sets its flag to prepared and replies with an acknowledgment, otherwise it replies with a reject.  
If the Coordinator receives acknowledgments from both participants, it sends a “commit” message; each participant then writes the confirmed surgery into its permanent schedule and clears the prepared flag.  
If any acknowledgment is missing because a participant crashes silently, the Coordinator times‑out and sends an “abort” message to the other participant, which then discards its prepared flag without modifying the permanent schedule.  
The Coordinator also records the outcome of each two‑phase transaction in a tiny log that can be inspected to recover from a crash.  

**SAFETY PROPERTY:** No surgery booking is ever added to the permanent schedules of the surgeon or the operating‑room without both the surgeon’s availability and the room’s calendar being updated together.

---- MODULE W4C0x2x1x0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* ---------- Constants ----------
CONSTANTS TIME_SLOTS, NoSlot \* NoSlot is a distinguished value not in TIME_SLOTS

\* ---------- Variables ----------
VARIABLES surgeonSched, roomSched,
          surgeonPrep, roomPrep,
          phase, curSlot,
          log

\* ---------- Helper definitions ----------
Idle   == "Idle"
Waiting== "Waiting"

\* ---------- Type invariant (optional, useful for debugging) ----------
TypeOK ==
    /\ surgeonSched \subseteq TIME_SLOTS
    /\ roomSched    \subseteq TIME_SLOTS
    /\ surgeonPrep \in BOOLEAN
    /\ roomPrep    \in BOOLEAN
    /\ phase       \in {Idle, Waiting}
    /\ curSlot     \in TIME_SLOTS \cup {NoSlot}
    /\ log \subseteq TIME_SLOTS \times {"commit","abort"}

\* ---------- Initial state ----------
Init ==
    /\ surgeonSched = {}
    /\ roomSched    = {}
    /\ surgeonPrep = FALSE
    /\ roomPrep    = FALSE
    /\ phase       = Idle
    /\ curSlot     = NoSlot
    /\ log         = {}

\* ---------- Actions ----------
Begin ==
    /\ phase   = Idle
    /\ curSlot = NoSlot
    /\ \E s \in TIME_SLOTS :
          /\ curSlot' = s
          /\ phase'    = Waiting
          /\ surgeonPrep' = FALSE
          /\ roomPrep'    = FALSE
          /\ UNCHANGED <<surgeonSched, roomSched, log>>

SurgeonPrepare ==
    /\ phase = Waiting
    /\ surgeonPrep = FALSE
    /\ curSlot \in TIME_SLOTS
    /\ curSlot \notin surgeonSched       \* slot must be free for the surgeon
    /\ surgeonPrep' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomPrep, surgeonSched, roomSched, phase, curSlot, log>>

RoomPrepare ==
    /\ phase = Waiting
    /\ roomPrep = FALSE
    /\ curSlot \in TIME_SLOTS
    /\ curSlot \notin roomSched          \* slot must be free for the room
    /\ roomPrep' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<surgeonPrep, surgeonSched, roomSched, phase, curSlot, log>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = Waiting
    /\ surgeonPrep = TRUE
    /\ roomPrep    = TRUE
    /\ curSlot \in TIME_SLOTS
    /\ surgeonSched' = surgeonSched \cup {curSlot}
    /\ roomSched'    = roomSched    \cup {curSlot}
    /\ surgeonPrep' = FALSE
    /\ roomPrep'    = FALSE
    /\ phase'       = Idle
    /\ curSlot'     = NoSlot
    /\ log'         = log \cup {<<curSlot, "commit">>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<>>

The system consists of a central Load‑Shed Controller, a set of Substation Agents that actually disconnect loads, and an Admin Console that can invoke an emergency override. Each participant keeps a tiny local state: the Controller holds a *coarse‑grid lock* indicating whether any load‑shed operation is in progress, each Substation Agent holds a *fine‑lock* that authorizes it to act on its own circuit, and the Admin Console holds an *override flag* that, when set, bypasses both locks. To begin shedding, the Controller first acquires the coarse‑grid lock; while it holds this lock it issues a request to a particular Substation Agent, which then attempts to acquire its fine‑lock. If the fine‑lock is granted, the Substation Agent disconnects the designated load and reports completion back to the Controller, which finally releases the coarse‑grid lock. The Admin Console may at any time set the override flag; when the flag is true the Controller automatically grants all fine‑locks and skips the coarse‑grid lock, allowing an immediate, pre‑emptive shed. After the override period ends, the flag is cleared and normal lock acquisition resumes. All lock acquisitions and releases are atomic messages sent over a reliable broadcast bus, ensuring that no two agents can hold conflicting locks simultaneously.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No load may be disconnected by a Substation Agent that does not currently hold both the global coarse‑grid lock (unless the admin override flag is set) and its own fine‑lock.

---- MODULE W4C9x8x6x5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANTS Substations, Loads, NoRequest

VARIABLES 
    coarseLock,          \* BOOL: true if the Controller holds the coarse‑grid lock
    fineLocks,          \* [Substations -> BOOLEAN] fine‑lock per substation
    overrideFlag,       \* BOOL: true if Admin override is active
    requestInProcess,   \* Substations \cup {NoRequest}: current substation request
    DisconnectedLoads,  \* SUBSET Loads: loads that have been shed
    AuthorizedDisconnect \* SUBSET Loads: loads that were shed under proper authorization

\* -------------------------- Initialization --------------------------

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = FALSE
    /\ overrideFlag = FALSE
    /\ requestInProcess = NoRequest
    /\ fineLocks = [s \in Substations |-> FALSE]
    /\ DisconnectedLoads = {}
    /\ AuthorizedDisconnect = {}

\* -------------------------- Actions --------------------------

\* Admin can enable override at any moment
AdminSetOverride ==
    /\ ~overrideFlag
    /\ overrideFlag' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, requestInProcess,
                   DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Admin can clear the override flag
AdminClearOverride ==
    /\ overrideFlag
    /\ overrideFlag' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, requestInProcess,
                   DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Controller acquires the coarse‑grid lock (only when no override)
ControllerAcquireCoarse ==
    /\ ~overrideFlag
    /\ ~coarseLock
    /\ coarseLock' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<overrideFlag, fineLocks, requestInProcess,
                   DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Controller releases the coarse‑grid lock (only when no pending request)
ControllerReleaseCoarse ==
    /\ coarseLock
    /\ requestInProcess = NoRequest
    /\ coarseLock' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<overrideFlag, fineLocks, requestInProcess,
                   DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Controller issues a shed request to a particular substation
ControllerRequestShed ==
    \E sub \in Substations :
        /\ ~overrideFlag
        /\ coarseLock
        /\ requestInProcess = NoRequest
        /\ requestInProcess' = sub
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, overrideFlag, fineLocks,
                       DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Substation acquires its fine‑lock in response to the request
SubstationAcquireFine ==
    \E sub \in Substations :
        /\ requestInProcess = sub
        /\ ~fineLocks[sub]
        /\ fineLocks' = [fineLocks EXCEPT ![sub] = TRUE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, overrideFlag, requestInProcess,
                       DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Substation disconnects a load (normal path – requires both locks)
SubstationDisconnectLoad ==
    \E sub \in Substations, load \in Loads :
        /\ requestInProcess = sub
        /\ fineLocks[sub]
        /\ load \notin DisconnectedLoads
        /\ (overrideFlag = TRUE) \/ (coarseLock = TRUE /\ fineLocks[sub] = TRUE)
        /\ DisconnectedLoads' = DisconnectedLoads \cup {load}
        /\ AuthorizedDisconnect' = AuthorizedDisconnect \cup {load}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, overrideFlag, requestInProcess>>

\* Substation reports completion, releasing its fine‑lock and clearing the request
SubstationReportCompletion ==
    \E sub \in Substations :
        /\ requestInProcess = sub
        /\ fineLocks[sub]
        /\ requestInProcess' = NoRequest
        /\ fineLocks' = [fineLocks EXCEPT ![sub] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, overrideFlag,
                       DisconnectedLoads, AuthorizedDisconnect>>

\* Immediate disconnect when override is active (controller automatically grants fine‑locks)
OverrideDisconnect ==
    \E sub \in Substations, load \in Loads :
        /\ overrideFlag
        /\ load \notin DisconnectedLoads
        /\ DisconnectedLoads' = DisconnectedLoads \cup {load}
        /\ AuthorizedDisconnect' = AuthorizedDisconnect \cup {load}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLocks, overrideFlag,
                       requestInProcess>>

\* -------------------------- Next State Relation --------------------------

Next ==
    \/ AdminSetOverride
    \/ AdminClearOverride
    \/ ControllerAcquireCoarse
    \/ ControllerReleaseCoarse
    \/ ControllerRequestShed
    \/ SubstationAcquireFine
    \/ SubstationDisconnectLoad
    \/ SubstationReportCompletion
    \/ OverrideDisconnect

\* -------------------------- Safety Invariant --------------------------

\* A load may appear in DisconnectedLoads only if it was authorized under the
\* required lock conditions (or the override flag).  The set AuthorizedDisconnect
\* records exactly those loads that were shed while the guard was satisfied.
SafetyInvariant ==
    DisconnectedLoads \subseteq AuthorizedDisconnect

\* -------------------------- Specification --------------------------

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, fineLocks, overrideFlag,
                         requestInProcess, DisconnectedLoads,
                         AuthorizedDisconnect>>

====
