The system consists of a fixed ring of settlement nodes, each representing a participating bank that can add settlement instructions to a shared inter‑bank batch. Each node keeps a local copy of three pieces of state: the identifier of the node that currently holds the exclusive token, the current size limit of the batch (the maximum slot number), and the next free slot number that the token‑holder is allowed to claim. When a node receives the token it may either (a) allocate the next free slot to one of its pending instructions, incrementing the next‑slot counter, or (b) forward the token unchanged if it has no work. A special Capacity Manager node can, at any moment, broadcast a capacity‑change message that adjusts the batch size limit up or down; all nodes update their local capacity variable immediately. If the capacity is reduced below the current next‑slot counter, the token‑holder must skip allocation until the counter is brought back within the new limit by rolling back uncommitted slots. After performing its action, the token‑holder passes the token to the next node in the ring, guaranteeing that only one node can allocate a slot at a time even while the capacity variable may be changing concurrently. The protocol terminates when the token makes a full rotation without any allocations and the next‑slot counter has reached the current capacity, indicating that the batch is full or no further work is pending.  

**SAFETY PROPERTY:** No two nodes ever allocate the same batch slot.
spec_text:
--------------------------- MODULE W4C3x1x3x4 ---------------------------

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* CONSTANTS *)
CONSTANT N          \* number of nodes in the ring (including the manager)
CONSTANT MaxCap     \* upper bound on the batch capacity used by the model

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* DEFINITIONS *)
Node == 1 .. N

NextNode(i) == IF i = N THEN 1 ELSE i + 1

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* VARIABLES *)
VARIABLES token, capacity, nextSlot, alloc

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* INITIAL STATE *)
Init ==
    /\ token = 1
    /\ capacity = MaxCap
    /\ nextSlot = 0
    /\ alloc = [s \in {} |-> 0]         \* empty partial function

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* ACTION: allocate the current free slot *)
Allocate ==
    /\ token \in Node
    /\ nextSlot < capacity
    /\ nextSlot \notin DOMAIN alloc
    /\ alloc' = [alloc EXCEPT ![nextSlot] = token]
    /\ nextSlot' = nextSlot + 1
    /\ token' = NextNode(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* ACTION: pass the token without allocating (e.g., no work or capacity limit) *)
Pass ==
    /\ token \in Node
    /\ token' = NextNode(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSlot, capacity, alloc>>

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* ACTION: rollback one uncommitted slot when capacity has been reduced *)
Rollback ==
    /\ token \in Node
    /\ nextSlot > capacity
    /\ LET s == nextSlot - 1 IN s \in DOMAIN alloc
    /\ alloc' = [t \in DOMAIN alloc \ {nextSlot - 1} |-> alloc[t]]
    /\ nextSlot' = nextSlot - 1
    /\ token' = NextNode(token)
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* ACTION: change the batch capacity (broadcast by the manager) *)
CapChange(newCap) ==
    /\ newCap \in 0 .. MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = newCap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, nextSlot, alloc>>

CapChangeAction ==
    \E newCap \in 0 .. MaxCap : CapChange(newCap)

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* NEXT STATE RELATION *)
Next ==
    \/ Allocate
    \/ Pass
    \/ Rollback
    \/ CapChangeAction

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* SAFETY INVARIANT: no two nodes ever allocate the same slot *)
NoDupSlotAlloc ==
    \A s1, s2 \in DOMAIN alloc :
        (alloc[s1] = alloc[s2]) => s1 = s2

(* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* THEOREM (for model checking) *)
THEOREM NoDupSlotAllocIsInvariant == 
    Init => []NoDupSlotAlloc

The system runs two registration servers, Server A and Server B, each serving a different campus but both drawing seats from a single shared pool for a popular class. Each server maintains a coarse‑lock flag that indicates whether it is currently processing a batch of enrollments, and a fine‑grained seat counter that records how many seats it has allocated in the current batch. When a student’s enrollment request arrives, the server first tries to acquire its coarse lock; if the lock is already held, the request is placed in a waiting queue. Once the coarse lock is secured, the server attempts to acquire a fine lock on a specific seat number; if that seat is already taken in the shared pool, the fine lock is released and another seat is tried. After successfully obtaining the fine lock, the server increments its local seat counter, decrements the global remaining‑seat count, and then releases the fine lock. When the server has finished all pending requests for the batch, it releases its coarse lock, allowing the other server to begin its own batch. Because the two servers never hold coarse locks at the same time and always release a fine lock before taking the next one, the shared pool’s seat count stays consistent across both instances.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of enrolled students never exceeds the total number of seats available for the course.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C8x8x4x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Servers, TotalSeats \* Servers = {"A","B"}; TotalSeats = a positive integer

(* ---------- State variables ---------- *)
VARIABLES coarseLock, localCount, available

(* ---------- Helper definitions ---------- *)
Seats == 1..TotalSeats

CoarseFree == \A s1, s2 \in Servers : s1 # s2 => ~(coarseLock[s1] /\ coarseLock[s2])

Allocated == TotalSeats - Cardinality(available)

(* ---------- Initial state ---------- *)
Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = [s \in Servers |-> FALSE]
    /\ localCount = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ available = Seats

(* ---------- Actions ---------- *)

(* A server acquires its coarse‑lock when no other server holds one *)
AcquireCoarse(s) ==
    /\ s \in Servers
    /\ ~coarseLock[s]
    /\ \A t \in Servers : t # s => ~coarseLock[t]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localCount, available>>

(* A server releases its coarse‑lock *)
ReleaseCoarse(s) ==
    /\ s \in Servers
    /\ coarseLock[s]
    /\ coarseLock' = [coarseLock EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localCount, available>>

(* While holding the coarse lock a server enrolls a student by taking a free seat *)
Enroll(s) ==
    /\ s \in Servers
    /\ coarseLock[s]
    /\ available # {}
    /\ \E seat \in available :
          /\ available' = available \ {seat}
          /\ localCount' = [localCount EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
          /\ UNCHANGED coarseLock

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : AcquireCoarse(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : ReleaseCoarse(s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Enroll(s)

(* ---------- Specification ---------- *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarseLock, localCount, available>>

(* ---------- Safety invariant (the property to check) ---------- *)
SeatSafety == Allocated <= TotalSeats

(* Optional: sanity invariants that help the model checker (not required for the task) *)
CoarseExclusion == CoarseFree

The lobby consists of a set of players who request to join a match, a Lobby Server that holds a lease on the match‑making resource, and a privileged Admin who can overwrite any lease. The server keeps three pieces of state: (1) the identifier of the player who currently holds the lease, (2) the timestamp at which that lease expires, and (3) the number of players already assigned to the pending match. When a player wishes to start matchmaking they send a lease‑request; if no lease is active or the current lease has expired, the server records that player as the new lease holder and sets the expiry to “now plus T” seconds. The lease holder must periodically send a lease‑renewal before expiry, which the server extends by another T seconds; failure to renew automatically relinquishes the lease. Any player may voluntarily release the lease, causing the server to clear the holder field and the expiry time. The Admin can issue an override command at any moment, which immediately replaces the current lease holder with the Admin’s chosen player and resets the expiry, regardless of existing lease state. After a lease is granted, the server increments the matched‑player count each time the holder confirms a teammate, rejecting further confirmations once the match capacity limit is reached.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of players assigned to a pending match never exceeds the match capacity.

------------------------------ MODULE W4C5x6x4x5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets, TLC

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* CONSTANTS *)
CONSTANTS 
    Players,            \* Set of player identifiers
    Admin,              \* Identifier of the privileged admin (unused in logic)
    T,                  \* Lease duration (in time units)
    Capacity,           \* Maximum number of players that can be assigned
    MaxTime             \* Upper bound on the logical clock for model checking

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* SPECIAL VALUE FOR NO CURRENT LEASE HOLDER *)
NoHolder == "None"

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* VARIABLES *)
VARIABLES 
    now,                \* Logical clock (0..MaxTime)
    leaseHolder,        \* Current lease holder ∈ Players ∪ {NoHolder}
    leaseExp,           \* Expiration time of the current lease (Nat)
    matchedCount        \* Number of players already assigned to the pending match

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* TYPE INVARIANT (helpful for debugging, not the safety property) *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ now \in 0..MaxTime
    /\ leaseHolder \in Players \cup {NoHolder}
    /\ leaseExp \in Nat
    /\ matchedCount \in Nat

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* INITIAL STATE *)
Init ==
    /\ now = 0
    /\ leaseHolder = NoHolder
    /\ leaseExp = 0
    /\ matchedCount = 0

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* ACTIONS *)

Request(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ (leaseHolder = NoHolder \/ leaseExp <= now)
    /\ leaseHolder' = p
    /\ leaseExp' = now + T
    /\ matchedCount' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED now

Renew(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ leaseHolder = p
    /\ leaseExp > now
    /\ leaseExp' = now + T
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, matchedCount, now>>

Release(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ leaseHolder = p
    /\ leaseHolder' = NoHolder
    /\ leaseExp' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<matchedCount, now>>

AdminOverride(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ leaseHolder' = p
    /\ leaseExp' = now + T
    /\ matchedCount' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED now

Confirm(p) ==
    /\ p \in Players
    /\ leaseHolder = p
    /\ leaseExp > now
    /\ matchedCount < Capacity
    /\ matchedCount' = matchedCount + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, leaseExp, now>>

Tick ==
    /\ now < MaxTime
    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseHolder, leaseExp, matchedCount>>

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* NEXT STATE RELATION *)
Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players: Request(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players: Renew(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players: Release(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players: Confirm(p)
    \/ \E p \in Players: AdminOverride(p)
    \/ Tick

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* SAFETY INVARIANT (the property we must check) *)
Safe ==
    matchedCount <= Capacity

(* --------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
(* SPECIFICATION *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<now, leaseHolder, leaseExp, matchedCount>>

The system consists of two dispenser instances, DispA and DispB, each serving a separate pharmacy counter but drawing medications from a single shared medication pool. The shared pool is represented by a counter “availableUnits” that records how many doses of a prescribed drug remain. Each dispenser keeps a local flag “requestPending” that indicates whether it is currently trying to allocate a dose. When a pharmacist enters a prescription, the corresponding dispenser sets its flag and reads the current value of “availableUnits”. It then performs a compare‑and‑swap on the shared register: if the read value is greater than zero, it attempts to replace it with the value minus one; the operation succeeds only for the first dispenser that issues it. A successful swap causes the dispenser to dispense the dose and clear its flag, while a failed swap makes the dispenser retry after a short back‑off. Because both dispensers use the same compare‑and‑swap register, at most one of them can decrement the pool for any given prescription, preventing double‑dispensing from the shared stock.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A dose that has been dispensed from the shared pool can never be dispensed again.

---- MODULE W4C16x7x5x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, TLC

CONSTANT InitUnits

VARIABLES availableUnits, pending, readVal, totalDispensed

\* The two dispenser identifiers
Dispenser == {"DispA", "DispB"}

\* Initial state
Init ==
    /\ availableUnits = InitUnits
    /\ pending = [d \in Dispenser |-> FALSE]
    /\ readVal = [d \in Dispenser |-> 0]
    /\ totalDispensed = 0

\* A pharmacist writes a prescription: the dispenser records that it has a pending request
\* and reads the current value of the shared counter.
EnterPrescription(d) ==
    /\ d \in Dispenser
    /\ pending[d] = FALSE
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = availableUnits]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<availableUnits, totalDispensed>>

\* Compare‑and‑swap succeeds: the value read is still current and > 0.
CASAttempt(d) ==
    /\ d \in Dispenser
    /\ pending[d] = TRUE
    /\ readVal[d] > 0
    /\ availableUnits = readVal[d]          \* CAS succeeds
    /\ availableUnits' = availableUnits - 1
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ totalDispensed' = totalDispensed + 1

\* Compare‑and‑swap fails (either value was 0 or another dispenser already changed it).
CASFail(d) ==
    /\ d \in Dispenser
    /\ pending[d] = TRUE
    /\ (readVal[d] = 0 \/ availableUnits # readVal[d])
    /\ pending' = pending
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = 0]   \* discard stale read, will retry later
    /\ UNCHANGED <<availableUnits, totalDispensed>>

\* The dispenser backs off and clears its flag; it may later start a new request.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ d \in Dispenser
    /\ pending[d] = TRUE
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<availableUnits, totalDispensed>>

\* The overall next‑state relation
Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Dispenser : EnterPrescription(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispenser : CASAttempt(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispenser : CASFail(d)
    \/ \E d \in Dispenser : Retry(d)

\* --------------------  Safety property  --------------------
\* A dose removed from the pool is never removed again.
InvSafety ==
    totalDispensed = InitUnits - availableUnits

\* (Optional type invariant – not used for model checking the safety property)
TypeOK ==
    /\ availableUnits \in Nat
    /\ pending \in [Dispenser -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ readVal \in [Dispenser -> Nat]
    /\ totalDispensed \in Nat

nl:
The conveyor line has three active participants: an entry sensor that detects a car arriving at the start, a wash‑station controller that moves the car through the brushes, and an exit gate that releases the car after washing. All three share a single compare‑and‑swap register that stores a “slot token’’ indicating whether the wash slot is free or occupied. When the entry sensor sees a car, it reads the current value of the register and attempts a compare‑and‑swap that changes the token from free to occupied; if the swap succeeds the sensor signals the controller to start moving the car onto the belt. The controller, after finishing the wash cycle, performs another compare‑and‑swap that changes the token from occupied back to free and then notifies the exit gate to open. Because messages (sensor‑to‑controller, controller‑to‑gate) can arrive out of order, each participant always checks the register’s current value before acting, so a stale “start” message will be ignored if the token is already occupied. The compare‑and‑swap operation itself is atomic, guaranteeing that at most one participant can claim the slot at any moment regardless of message reordering. When the exit gate receives a free‑token notification, it only opens if it sees that the token is indeed free, preventing a car from leaving before the wash is complete. Thus the whole line progresses safely even though network delays may shuffle the ordering of the messages.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: A car can be released by the exit gate at most once for each wash cycle.

---- MODULE W4C4x7x5x1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, TLC

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Constants
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
TokenSet == {"Free", "Occupied"}
MsgSet   == {"Start", "Free"}

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Variables
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
VARIABLES token, msgs, opened

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Type invariant (helpful for debugging, not part of the safety property)
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in TokenSet
    /\ msgs \subseteq MsgSet
    /\ opened \in BOOLEAN

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Initial state
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Init ==
    /\ token = "Free"
    /\ msgs = {}
    /\ opened = FALSE

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Actions
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)

(* Sensor reads the register and successfully swaps Free → Occupied *)
SensorCAS_Success ==
    /\ token = "Free"
    /\ token' = "Occupied"
    /\ opened' = FALSE
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {"Start"}

(* Sensor attempts CAS but sees the slot already occupied – nothing happens *)
SensorCAS_Fail ==
    /\ token # "Free"
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, msgs, opened >>

(* Delivery of the start message to the controller; the controller may ignore it *)
DeliverStart ==
    /\ "Start" \in msgs
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {"Start"}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, opened >>

(* Controller finishes washing, swaps Occupied → Free and notifies the gate *)
ControllerFinish ==
    /\ token = "Occupied"
    /\ token' = "Free"
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {"Free"}
    /\ UNCHANGED opened

(* Delivery of a free‑token notification that the gate ignores (e.g., stale) *)
DeliverFreeNoOp ==
    /\ "Free" \in msgs
    /\ (token # "Free" \/ opened = TRUE)
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {"Free"}
    /\ UNCHANGED << token, opened >>

(* Gate opens when it sees a free token and has not opened yet in the current cycle *)
GateOpen ==
    /\ "Free" \in msgs
    /\ token = "Free"
    /\ opened = FALSE
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {"Free"}
    /\ opened' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED token

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Next-state relation
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Next ==
    \/ SensorCAS_Success
    \/ SensorCAS_Fail
    \/ DeliverStart
    \/ ControllerFinish
    \/ DeliverFreeNoOp
    \/ GateOpen

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Specification
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, msgs, opened>>

(* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
   Safety invariant: at most one release (gate opening) per wash cycle
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------- *)
NoDoubleRelease ==
    /\ (token = "Occupied") => (opened = FALSE)
    /\ (opened = TRUE)      => (token = "Free")

The system consists of two runway‑allocation servers, one for domestic flights and one for international flights, that both draw from a single pool of time‑stamped runway slots. Each server keeps a local copy of the shared allocation record, which lists the next free slot and a version counter that identifies the latest update. When a server receives a request for a slot, it reads the current record, chooses the earliest free slot, increments the version counter, and attempts to write the new record back using a compare‑and‑swap operation on the shared register. The compare‑and‑swap succeeds only if the version counter in the register still matches the one the server read; otherwise the server discards its tentative allocation and retries from the updated record. Both servers repeat this loop until their allocation is committed, guaranteeing that at most one server can claim a particular slot at any moment. The shared register therefore serialises the two independent instances without any additional locking mechanism. Because each successful compare‑and‑swap overwrites the previous record atomically, the pool of runway slots remains consistent across both instances.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No runway‑slot allocation record can be overwritten without preserving the most recent assignment, preventing any lost updates to the shared schedule.

---- MODULE W4C1x7x1x2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANT MaxSlot \* maximum slot index (bounds the state space)

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Variables
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
VARIABLES shared, lDom, lInt

\* Record containing the next free slot and a version counter
SharedRec == [slot |-> Nat, ver |-> Nat]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Initial state
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Init ==
    /\ shared = [slot |-> 0, ver |-> 0]
    /\ lDom   = [slot |-> 0, ver |-> 0]
    /\ lInt   = [slot |-> 0, ver |-> 0]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Helper: compute the next record that a server would try to commit
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
NextRec(rec) ==
    [slot |-> rec.slot + 1,
     ver  |-> rec.ver  + 1]

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Server actions
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Domestic server reads the shared record into its local copy
DomRead ==
    /\ UNCHANGED shared
    /\ lDom' = shared
    /\ lInt' = lInt

\* Domestic server attempts a compare‑and‑swap
DomCAS ==
    /\ IF shared.ver = lDom.ver
          THEN /\ shared' = NextRec(shared)
               /\ lDom'   = lDom   \* keep local copy (it will be refreshed on next read)
          ELSE /\ shared' = shared
               /\ lDom'   = lDom
    /\ lInt' = lInt
    /\ shared.slot < MaxSlot   \* stop allocating after MaxSlot‑1

\* International server reads the shared record
IntRead ==
    /\ UNCHANGED shared
    /\ lInt' = shared
    /\ lDom' = lDom

\* International server attempts a compare‑and‑swap
IntCAS ==
    /\ IF shared.ver = lInt.ver
          THEN /\ shared' = NextRec(shared)
               /\ lInt'   = lInt
          ELSE /\ shared' = shared
               /\ lInt'   = lInt
    /\ lDom' = lDom
    /\ shared.slot < MaxSlot

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Next‑state relation
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Next ==
    \/ DomRead
    \/ DomCAS
    \/ IntRead
    \/ IntCAS

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Safety invariant (the property to be model‑checked)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* No runway‑slot allocation record can be overwritten without preserving
\* the most recent assignment.  This is captured by requiring that the
\* version counter and the slot index are always equal.  Because each
\* successful compare‑and‑swap increments both by exactly one, equality
\* guarantees that no update can lose the previous assignment.
NoLostUpdate ==
    shared.slot = shared.ver

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Specification
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<shared, lDom, lInt>>

\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
\* Theorems (optional, for readability)
\* ----------------------------------------------------------------------
THEOREM Spec => []NoLostUpdate

====

Each controller maintains a local flag `want` indicating whether it is trying to claim the next block, and a shared compare‑and‑swap register `Token` that either holds the identifier of the controller currently owning a token or is empty. When a controller needs the next block, it sets its `want` flag true and atomically executes a compare‑and‑swap on `Token`, swapping an empty value for its own identifier only if the register is still empty. If the swap succeeds, the controller treats the token as granted and proceeds to reserve the block; if it fails, it repeatedly retries after a short back‑off while keeping its `want` flag set. When the controller releases the block, it clears its `want` flag and performs a compare‑and‑swap that replaces its identifier in `Token` with the empty value, making the token available to the other instance. Because both controllers use the same register, only one can succeed in the compare‑and‑swap at a time, ensuring that the single token is never duplicated. The protocol therefore requires only two state variables per controller (`want`) and one shared variable (`Token`).  

SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time can both controllers hold a block‑allocation token for the same track segment simultaneously.

The fleet consists of autonomous robots that need to reserve a storage slot before moving goods, and a lightweight central controller that hosts a single compare‑and‑swap register for each slot. Each robot keeps two pieces of state: the identifier of the slot it is trying to reserve and a flag indicating whether it has successfully claimed that slot. When a robot wants a slot, it reads the slot’s register; if the register currently holds the value “free”, the robot attempts a compare‑and‑swap changing the value from “free” to its own robot identifier. If the compare‑and‑swap succeeds, the robot marks its flag as claimed and proceeds to the slot; if it fails because another robot has already written its identifier, the robot picks a different slot and repeats the process. Because a robot may be arbitrarily slow after a successful claim, the compare‑and‑swap still prevents any other robot from writing the same identifier to that register, allowing other robots to allocate different slots without waiting for the slow robot to finish its movement. The central controller never removes a robot’s identifier from a slot register until the robot explicitly releases the slot after completing its task.  

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two robots can ever be assigned the same storage slot at the same time.

---- MODULE W4C2x7x3x3 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Slots

(*--- Constants for special values ---*)
Free == "free"
Null == "none"

VARIABLES reg, claimed, desiredSlot

(*--- Initialization ---*)
Init ==
  /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
  /\ claimed = [r \in Robots |-> FALSE]
  /\ desiredSlot = [r \in Robots |-> Null]

(*--- Robot tries to reserve a free slot ---*)
TryReserve(r) ==
  \E s \in Slots :
    /\ reg[s] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ desiredSlot' = [desiredSlot EXCEPT ![r] = s]

(*--- Robot releases a slot it has claimed ---*)
Release(r) ==
  /\ claimed[r] = TRUE
  /\ LET s == desiredSlot[r] IN
       /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
       /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
       /\ desiredSlot' = [desiredSlot EXCEPT ![r] = Null]

(*--- Next-state relation ---*)
Next ==
  \E r \in Robots :
       TryReserve(r) \/ Release(r)

(*--- Temporal specification ---*)
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, claimed, desiredSlot>>

(*--- Safety invariant: no two robots claim the same slot at the same time ---*)
NoConflictingClaims ==
  \A r1, r2 \in Robots :
    (r1 # r2) => ~(claimed[r1] /\ claimed[r2] /\ desiredSlot[r1] = desiredSlot[r2])

The yard contains several gantry cranes, each identified by a unique crane‑id, and a single high‑value container that must be moved from the ship to a storage stack. Each crane stores locally a flag called `busy` indicating whether it currently believes it owns the container, and the yard maintains a single compare‑and‑swap (CAS) register whose value is either “free” or the id of the crane that most recently succeeded in claiming the container. When a crane wants to lift the container it reads the CAS register; if the value is “free” it attempts a CAS operation that changes the register from “free” to its own id, and only if the CAS succeeds does it set its local `busy` flag to true and begin the lift. After the lift is finished the crane writes “free” back to the CAS register and clears its `busy` flag, making the container available again. If a crane reads the register and sees another id, it simply waits and retries later, which tolerates a slow crane because the register is never cleared by a failed or delayed participant. The protocol therefore requires only the CAS register and each crane’s `busy` flag, giving a model with two state variables per crane and one shared variable.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two cranes can be busy with the same container at the same time.
spec_text:
---- MODULE W4C7x7x0x3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

\* ---------- Constants ----------
CONSTANT NumCrane               \* number of cranes in the yard
ASSUME NumCrane \in Nat \ {0}

Cranes == 1 .. NumCrane          \* the set of crane identifiers
Free   == 0                     \* special value meaning “container is free”

\* ---------- Variables ----------
VARIABLES cas, busy              \* cas register and per‑crane busy flags

\* ---------- Initial state ----------
Init ==
    /\ cas = Free
    /\ busy = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]

\* ---------- Actions ----------
Claim(c) ==
    /\ c \in Cranes
    /\ cas = Free
    /\ ~busy[c]                     \* the crane does not already think it owns the container
    /\ cas' = c
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]

Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in Cranes
    /\ busy[c]                      \* the crane believes it owns the container
    /\ cas = c
    /\ cas' = Free
    /\ busy' = [busy EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]

Wait(c) ==
    /\ c \in Cranes
    /\ cas # Free
    /\ ~busy[c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cas, busy>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes: Claim(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes: Release(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes: Wait(c)

\* ---------- Specification ----------
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<cas, busy>>

\* ---------- Safety property ----------
BusySet == {c \in Cranes : busy[c]}

NoTwoBusy == Cardinality(BusySet) <= 1
\* (equivalently: \A c1, c2 \in Cranes : (busy[c1] /\ busy[c2]) => c1 = c2)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoTwoBusy
